NTNU Open Call 2 Offer  

The DigiWind NTNU Open Call 2 presents a valuable opportunity for students aspiring to advance their digital skills through international placement in fields related to the digitalisation of wind and energy systems. 

Through this call, up to fifteen (15) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their exchange stay in Norway during either Spring or Autumn Semester of 2027. 

  1. Award type: Scholarships are provided as stipend to cover living and subsistence costs during the 6-months-exchange period. 
  2. Financial value: Each selected beneficiary will receive a stipend of EUR 6,940. 
  3. Tuition fees: Exchange students from NTNU’s partner universities are exempt from tuition fees in accordance with NTNU Regulations.  
  4. Welfare fee: All students are required to pay a mandatory welfare fee of approximately 70 EUR per semester, which must be covered personally by the applicant. This one-time payment is due by February 1st for Spring semester and September 1st for Autumn semester, and detailed instructions regarding the payment process will be provided by the NTNU International Office as part of the formal admission and enrolment procedure. 
  5. Payment mechanism: Stipends may be distributed via cash cards provided by NTNU’s Unit for International Relations for use within Norway. Disbursement is subject to signing the mobility agreement, confirmation of enrolment, and compliance with all eligibility and reporting requirements outlined in the Open Call. 
  6. Call interdependency: Autumn 2027 scholarships will be funded from the remaining funds after Spring 2027 cut-off, which makes it dependant on the number of candidates successful for the Spring 2027 call.  

Applicants profile 

DigiWind scholarships are available for students undertaking a 6-month study period at NTNU and enrolling in courses within the following eligible M.Sc. programmes: M.Sc. Electric Power Engineering and M.Sc. Marine Technology. 

Applicants must be final year students or hold one of the following degrees obtained at an internationally recognised university or higher education institution: 

  1. Bachelor of Science in Engineering (B.Sc. Eng.). 
  2. Bachelor of Engineering (B.Eng.). 
  3. Bachelor of Natural Science (B.Sc.). 

Applicants must have a background within a relevant field of engineering to meet the prerequisites of the M.Sc. Electric Power Engineering or M.Sc. Marine Technology courses. 

Eligible candidates must be passport holders from EU/EEA countries, or Digital Europe Programme (DEP) associated countries and demonstrate their active student status through an official Certificate of Enrolment for the current academic year in a NTNU partner university.  

Proficiency in English is a fundamental requirement, as it is the official language of both the Open Call and the master's programme. Unless the applicant is a native speaker, they must provide a certified score report meeting minimum thresholds: an IELTS Academic score of 6.5, a TOEFL iBT score of 88, or a Cambridge English (C1/C2) score of 180.  

Candidates are expected to be organized and detail-oriented, ensuring that all necessary documentation is submitted via the F6S platform for the Spring semester by the November 2nd, 2026, or for the Autumn semester by the 1 March 2027 deadline. 

Beyond technical qualifications, successful applicants will reflect DigiWind and NTNU’s core commitment to diversity, social equality, and gender balance. We particularly encourage applications from women and individuals from economically disadvantaged or diverse demographic backgrounds who seek to contribute to the wind energy field.  

Evaluation process  

Submission will be done EXCLUSIVELY via F6S platform Spring 2027 or Autumn 2027. Students are allowed to apply to only one of the semesters (either Spring 2027 or Autumn 2027).  

A complete list of applicants will be compiled, including basic information for statistical and transparency purposes (which will be also shared with the European Commission). 

Applications that pass the eligibility check will undergo an internal evaluation, conducted by a panel of experts from NTNU. For more information on the selection and evaluation process please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants.  

Results notification 

Following the expert’s evaluation, all eligible applicants will be ranked according to their final assessment scores. Scholarships will be awarded based on this order of merit, beginning with the highest-ranked candidates. 

Evaluation results will be compiled into an Evaluation Summary Report. Applicants will be notified of the results via email, as follows: 

  1. For Accepted Applicants: 
  2. An Evaluation Summary Report. 
  3. An invitation to proceed to the enrolment phase and following steps. 
  4. For Rejected Applicants: 
  5. An Evaluation Summary Report for those who passed the eligibility check and underwent internal evaluation phase. 
  6. A rejection letter to ineligible applications. 

Successful applicants must confirm their acceptance of the formal scholarship offer within five (5) business days by replying to the DigiWind NTNU Open Call team at ntnu-opencall@digiwind.org.  

For more details, please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants. 

Redress process 

Applicants who are not satisfied with the evaluation of their application, may submit a written appeal within three (3) business days of receiving their result. Appeals will be reviewed by a panel, chaired by the NTNU DigiWind representative, the Project Officer and one external member.  

Appeals are typically not allowed for disagreements with the academic judgment (score) or if the decision was based on the applicants misunderstanding of the application instructions. Valid grounds for appealing scholarships offer decision generally focus on errors in the assessment process or claims of discrimination. 

All requests for appeal must be sent to the DigiWind NTNU Open Call team at ntnu-opencall@digiwind.org

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. Aim of the One Semester Exchange Scholarships

The aim of the One Semester Exchange Scholarships (hereinafter referred to as the SCHOLARSHIPS) is to support students in completing their full curriculum through a one semester exchange at the University of Pavia (Italy) or the University of Vaasa (Finland), thereby extending their knowledge and skills in advanced digital technologies (one of the DIGI-ME target areas).

2. DIGI-ME Scholarships 

The SCHOLARSHIPS are granted by the DIGI-ME project. The DIGI-ME project is co-funded by the European Union under Grant Agreement No. 101123009. Up to EUR 21,000 is available to be distributed through targeted scholarships at Grenoble Ecole de Management (hereinafter referred to as GEM). Through this call, up to three (3) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their participation in the DIGI-ME path of a one semester exchange with the University of Pavia, and up to three (3) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their participation in the DIGI-ME path of a one semester exchange with the University of Vaasa. 

3. Financial value 

3.1 Scholarships are provided as a lump sum to support students in paying their tuition fees during the semester exchange. Each selected beneficiary will receive a lump sum for a single mobility action of up to four (4) months, taking place within the period from January 2027 to June 2027, at either the University of Pavia (Italy) or the University of Vaasa (Finland). 

The scholarship comprises a minimum of one component (Item A) and a maximum of two components (Items A and B). 

3.1.1 Fixed component 

Item A: Total contribution towards tuition fees: EUR 3,000 (one-time payment). 

3.1.2 Additional component based on special conditions 

Item B: Additional contribution towards tuition fees for participants with fewer opportunities: EUR 500 (one-time payment). 

Participants with fewer opportunities are defined as students who, prior to the start of the mobility period, meet one or more of the following criteria: 

  1. Are recipients of the French national student grant (CROUS) and belong to one of the four highest grant levels (levels 4, 5, 6, or 7); 
  2. Have a disability with a certified degree of invalidity of at least 50%; 
  3. Hold refugee status and/or benefit from international or subsidiary protection, or are displaced persons; 
  4. Have dependent minor children (students who have given birth to a child during the 2026–2027 academic year, as proven by a birth certificate, up to the child’s first birthday); 
  5. Are engaged in employment (students employed, other than occasionally and not by a family member up to and including the second degree, for a period of at least six months within the 12 months preceding the mobility period, in documented employment, self-employment, or professional activity in the public or private sector); 
  6. Are recognised professional athletes (students who are athletes of national interest must present a certificate from the relevant sports federation); 
  7. Are orphans of at least one parent (a student is considered an orphan if their father and/or mother died before the date of submission of the mobility application. This status is recognised provided that the student: (a) is under 26 years of age at the time of application, and/or (b) was financially dependent on the deceased parent at the time of death or is in a similarly economically dependent situation); 
  8. Are children of victims of terrorism or organised crime. 

Supporting documents for Item B will be requested only from successful applicants. 

4. Payment mechanism 

4.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is paid in two instalments: 

4.1.1 The first instalment, equal to 80% of the total estimated scholarship amount, will be paid within 30 days of signing the Mobility Agreement, provided that the student: 

Has submitted a Learning Agreement duly approved and signed by GEM and the host Higher Education Institution; 

Has correctly entered their bank details in the designated system. 

If any of the above conditions are not met, payment of the first instalment will be made within 30 days of their fulfilment. 

4.1.2 The second instalment, representing the remaining 20%, will be paid at the end of the mobility period, subject to verification of: 

  1. Fulfilment of the administrative and procedural obligations set out in this call; 
  2. Successful completion of the authorised mobility period; 
  3. Achievement of learning outcomes consistent with the Learning Agreement; 
  4. Proper administrative completion of the mobility period, including a duly signed certificate of arrival and a duly signed certificate of departure. 

Failure to comply with any of the above conditions may result in the loss of entitlement to the final payment and may lead to the total or partial recovery of sums already received.

Beneficiaries are solely responsible for determining any personal tax obligations and, where necessary, for making any required declarations to the competent tax authorities.

For more information, please refer to the French tax administration impots.gouv.fr or service-public.fr. 

5. Evaluation process 

Applications must be submitted EXCLUSIVELY through the dedicated form from 18 September 2026 (09:00, Brussels time) to 18 November 2026 (18:00, Brussels time). A complete list of applicants will be compiled, including basic information for statistical and transparency purposes, and may be shared with the European Commission. Applications that pass the eligibility check will undergo an internal evaluation, conducted by a panel of three experts from GEM. For more information on the selection and evaluation process, please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants (Annex 1). The following applicants are eligible: 

6.1 Students regularly enrolled at GEM at master’s level (M1 or M2). Applicants must be: 

  1. Enrolled for the academic year 2026–2027; 
  2. Full-time students; 
  3. Not on academic leave. 

6.2 Citizens of the European Union (hereinafter referred to as the EU) or of eligible DEP countries (the full list is available here: list-3rd-country-participation_digital_en.pdf).

  1. TOEFL iBT: 80; 
  2. IELTS Academic / IELTS Indicator: 6.0; 
  3. Cambridge English (Proficiency, Advanced, or Business Higher): Grade A, B, or C; 
  4. Duolingo English Test: 100; 
  5. Bachelor’s degree fully taught in English (official proof required).

Hence, the scholarship covered by this call is incompatible with any other EU funding allocated for the same purpose. Applicants must declare that they have not received other European Union funding for the same purpose in the dedicated form. 

7. Required documents 

7.1 Transcripts of records: full higher education transcripts to date, showing passed examinations and related grades. 

7.2 Curriculum vitae (CV): detailed CV outlining academic history, professional experience, skills, and relevant achievements (no photo required; maximum 1 page). 

7.3 Personal statement / motivation letter: statement (maximum 1 page) explaining the applicant’s motivation, interest in the programme, and how their background aligns with the DIGI-ME path of a one semester exchange at the University of Pavia or the University of Vaasa. 

7.4 English language competency: certified evidence of English proficiency meeting the specified minimum scores above. 

7.5 Copy of passport or ID card: copy of a valid passport or identity card. 

7.6 Optional: information on gender, age, and socio-economic status. In the event of equal scores, these factors may be positively considered during evaluation, in line with GEM’s commitment to supporting a diverse student body. 

8. Evaluation criteria and scoring 

8.1 Only eligible candidates will be evaluated. Successful candidates must reach an evaluation threshold of 70%. 

8.2 Applications will be assessed as follows: 

  1. Academic background (65%): based on the weighted average grade and adjusted by the ratio of earned to expected ECTS credits. 
  2. Motivation (25%): reflects the applicant’s commitment to developing advanced digital skills in innovation, international business, and entrepreneurship, as demonstrated in the motivation letter. 
  3. Additional experience (10%): considers academic and non-academic achievements reported in the applicant’s CV. 

8.3 DIGI-ME and GEM are committed to promoting diversity, social and economic equality, and gender balance in all aspects of this open call. As part of our selection process, applicants will have the option to provide information on gender, age, and socio-economic background. In the event of equal scores, priority will be given in the following order: 

  1. Female applicants; 
  2. Applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds; 
  3. Applicants with disabilities; 
  4. Applicants from countries with a low Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI) score; 
  5. Applicants belonging to minority groups.

Following evaluation by the expert panel, eligible applicants will be ranked according to their final assessment scores. Scholarships will be awarded based on this order of merit, beginning with the highest-ranked candidates. Applicants who meet the evaluation threshold but fall below the cut-off will be placed on a reserve list, ranked by score, and may receive an offer if a selected candidate declines or fails to accept within the stated deadline. All requests for appeal must be sent to GEM Global – DIGI-ME Section at digime.mobility@grenoble-em.com.

These purposes involve the communication of data to bodies external to Grenoble Ecole de Management (EU Agencies, host institution), as required by current European legislation General Data Protection Regulation no. 2016/679 art. 13.

1.Summary and purpose of the call

The Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya – Barcelona TECH (hereinafter “UPC”) is soliciting applications for scholarships grants (hereinafter “scholarships”) to support students of the master's degree program “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI Master”) taught at UPC Castelldefels School of Telecommunications and Aerospace Engineering (hereinafter “EETAC”) in Castelldefels, Spain

The UPC- AI4CI scholarships is granted by the “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI project”). The AI4CI project is co-funded by the European Union within the under the Grant Agreement No. 101123524 funded under the topic DIGITAL-2022-SKILLS-03-SPECIALISED-EDU - Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas.

The maximum funding available under this call is €167,500 and may be awarded until the available budget is fully exhausted, provided that this occurs within the overall implementation period of the AI4CI project.

The indicative total number of scholarships to be awarded is approximately 49 ranging from 500 EUR to 4,500 EUR.

The aim of the scholarships is that recipients benefit from AI4CI project's high-quality education in digital areas and to promote equality and excellence in the field of computer science and AI, as well as to increase the accessibility of master's studies developing advanced digital skills and promote the growth of higher-level skills, equality and diversity in computer science.

Converging towards gender equality in ICT fields in EU and the socioeconomic status of the applicant are factors that will be taken into account in the selection process but everyone is welcome to apply regardless their gender and/or socioeconomic situation

This call covers the cohorts 2025-2027 and 2026-2028.

2. Characteristics of support

The scholarship will be awarded to persons (hereinafter referred to as applicants) who are citizens of the European Union, listed EEA countries or of countries associated to Digital Europe Programme and who are currently studying in the AI4CI project master's degree program “AI4CI Master” at “EETAC” in Castelldefels, Spain; as well as those students who have already been pre-admitted to the “AI4CI Master” (2026-2027) and are expected to complete their enrolment in the coming weeks and those who will be admitted to the “AI4CI Master” for the course 2027-2028.

This call offers 4 different support modalities, as described below. Applicants may apply for a combination of different support modalities. However, regardless of the combination of modalities requested, the maximum aggregate scholarship amount that may be awarded to any eligible student is 4.500€.

The maximum amount specified for each modality applies only to that specific modality. Therefore, while different modalities may be combined, the total scholarship amount awarded to any individual student shall not exceed 4.500€. Consequently, no student may receive the maximum amount available under all four modalities simultaneously.

2.1 Reimbursement of tuition fees

Reimbursement of tuition fees includes:                         

  1. The enrollment tuition costs for the full master's program which must be paid before the end of the project.
  2. Administrative and support fees.
  3. The cost of issuance of the official title (if paid before the end of the project)

Each EU beneficiary can be reimbursed up to a maximum of 3.400€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required.

2.2 Contribution to living and transportation expenses

The scholarship supports living and/or transportation expenses. In particular, it covers a monthly allowance of 100 € for a maximum of 6 months between the resolution of the concession and the end of the project.

Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 600€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.

2.3 Contribution to expenses for mobility stays related to the master program

The scholarship supports expenses for in person mobility stays not covered by the Erasmus+ Program related to the AI4CI master program. They must be incurred while the student is enrolled in the program and before the end of the project.

In particular, it supports living, transportation and accommodation expenses related to study collaboration visit to another institution, academic stay at another institution for the master thesis or attendance to courses taught at another university within the framework of the master program.

Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 500€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.

2.4 Other study-related expenses

The scholarship supports expenses for the purchase of hardware and/or software necessary to study; for the acquisition of additional training or information sources, improvement of the necessary competencies and for other study-related expenses. The maximum amount for this modality is up to 1.100€.

3.    Requirements for applicants

1.  Candidates must have been already admitted to the AI4CI master at UPC EETAC or applied to be admitted for the academic year. This means that to be considered for the scholarship, applicants must apply concurrently to the master's program for the cohort 2026-2028 or be already enrolled in the program from the cohort 2025-2027.

2.  Being a full-time degree-seeking student in the AI4CI master's degree program (corresponding to 30 ECTS per semester).

3.  To be an EU citizen or a citizen of one of the listed EEA countries or of one of the countries associated to Digital Europe Programme – provide a copy of the identity document indicating nationality;

4.  For modality 2.2, having monthly rental expenses of at least 200€ or living at a distance of UPC Castelldefels of at least 20 km.

5.For modality 2. 3, the expenses have to be related to the AI4CI master program.

6.  For modality 2.4 a justification letter together with the corresponding quotation(s) dated within the previous 15 days to the application and final related invoices and proof of payments.

4.    Applications

Applications may be submitted according to the following cut-off dates, provided that the maximum available budget has not been exhausted:

  1. 29th September 2026 (23:59h Brussels time).
  2. 5th February 2027 (23:59h Brussels time).
  3. 5th July 2027 (23:59h Brussels time).

The application must be submitted through the UPC Electronic Office filling in the UPC-AI4CI scholarships form. The link is as follows: https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/.

The following documentation has to be attached to the application form:

  1. Cover letter stating the following: presentation of the candidate detailing their academic merits, the motivation and plans, how the received scholarship will be used, how it will contribute to the student’s upskilling in advanced digital skills, and the description of their socioeconomic situation (personal, social, economic, work, etc.) that may be relevant to obtaining the scholarship (mandatory for all modalities);
  2. Documentary evidence of the situations described in the previous point (mandatory for all modalities);
  3. A copy of the identity document showing the date of birth and nationality of the applicant (mandatory for all modalities);
  4. For modality 2.2 also provide documentary evidence of meeting the rental or distance requirements established in point 3.4.
  5. For modality 2.3 also provide information about the mobility stay, letter explaining the purpose and relationship with the master program and budget.
  6. For modality 2.4 also provide information about the hardware or software purpose of study plus a quotation dated within the previous 15 days to the application and the corresponding invoices and proof of payments. The same will apply with regard to the acquisition of additional or information sources towards the improvement of the necessary competencies or other study-related expenses not covered by modalities 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3.

5.     Selection criteria

The selection committee (please refer to clause 7) will evaluate the applications taking into account the academic merit of the candidate as well as the gender and socioeconomic disparities in engineering and computer science.

For modality 2.3, the relationship of the expenses with the AI4CI master program will be checked.

In particular, per each modality, a formula of 8 points based on academic merit and 2 points for gender and socioeconomic situation (1 point if female and 1 point if last year annual income has been less than 21.000€ per year) for a total of 10 points will be assigned to each candidate based on the information candidates provide to the committee. Both the master's program application documents and the additional documentation provided for this scholarship application will be taken into account.

Applications that fulfill the eligibility criteria but are not awarded because of budget limitations will be included in a reserve list (one per each modality). In case one of the awarded candidates can’t accept or refuses the scholarship or loses the financial support, the first candidate in the corresponding reserve list will be automatically re-considered for assessment.

6.    Resolution

Applications for modalities 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 will be continuously assessed.

Within 5 working days after the reception of applications, the selection committee assesses the received applications, their suitability, award points according to the criteria set out in clause 5 and thus rank the applicants. The selection committee selects the best-ranked applicants, but only those who fully meet the Scholarship requirements described in this call.

Scholarship resolutions related to this call will be published through UPC’s Electronic Notice Board (https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/ca/etauler/e-tauler), “e-Tauler”. and will be communicated to all candidates by the selection committee by e-mail on the same day the resolutions are published. All information about awarded scholarships will be published at the UPC-AI4CI Scholarship website.

7.    Payment conditions

Payments related to each modality will be done according to the following schedule, namely:

1. Awarded students coming from the cohort 2025-2027:

  1. 1st Instalment: 21st October 2026.
  2. 2nd Instalment: 29th February 2027.
  3. 2nd Instalment: 30th July 2027.

2. Awarded students coming from the cohort 2026-2028:

  1. 1st Instalment: 29th February 2027.

The UPC- AI4CI scholarships is granted by the “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI project”). The AI4CI project is co-funded by the European Union within the under the Grant Agreement No. 101123524 funded under the topic DIGITAL-2022-SKILLS-03-SPECIALISED-EDU - Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas.

The maximum funding available under this call is €167,500 and may be awarded until the available budget is fully exhausted, provided that this occurs within the overall implementation period of the AI4CI project.

The indicative total number of scholarships to be awarded is approximately 49 ranging from 500 EUR to 4,500 EUR.

The aim of the scholarships is that recipients benefit from AI4CI project's high-quality education in digital areas and to promote equality and excellence in the field of computer science and AI, as well as to increase the accessibility of master's studies developing advanced digital skills and promote the growth of higher-level skills, equality and diversity in computer science.

Converging towards gender equality in ICT fields in EU and the socioeconomic status of the applicant are factors that will be taken into account in the selection process but everyone is welcome to apply regardless their gender and/or socioeconomic situation

This call covers the cohorts 2025-2027 and 2026-2028.

Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 500€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.

results.content: DIGI-ME Triple Degree Scholarship Award Procedure and Selection Rules at Grenoble Ecole de Management (EESC - GEM)

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. Aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships

The aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships (hereinafter referred to as the SCHOLARSHIPS) is to support students in completing their full curriculum through a triple degree programme at the University of Pavia and the University of Vaasa, thereby extending their knowledge and skills in advanced digital technologies (one of the DIGI-ME target areas). 

2. DIGI-ME Scholarships 

The SCHOLARSHIPS are granted by the DIGI-ME project. The DIGI-ME project is co-funded by the European Union under Grant Agreement No. 101123009. Up to EUR 100,000 is available to be distributed through targeted scholarships at Grenoble Ecole de Management (hereinafter referred to as GEM). Through this call, up to ten (10) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their participation in the DIGI-ME path of the triple degree programme with the University of Pavia and the University of Vaasa. 

3. Financial value 

3.1 Scholarships are provided as a lump sum to support students in paying their tuition fees during the triple degree exchange programme. Each selected beneficiary will receive a lump sum for two mobility periods totalling 8 to 10 months, depending on the individual Learning Agreement, in the period from January 2027 to May 2027 at the University of Pavia (Italy) and from January 2028 to May 2028 at the University of Vaasa (Finland). 

The scholarship comprises a minimum of one component (Item A) and a maximum of two components (Items A and B). 

3.1.1 Fixed component 

Item A: Total contribution towards tuition fees: EUR 8,000 (one-time payment). 

3.1.2 Additional component based on special conditions 

Item B: Additional contribution towards tuition fees for participants with fewer opportunities: EUR 2,000 (one-time payment). 

Participants with fewer opportunities are defined as students who, prior to the start of the mobility period, meet one or more of the following criteria: 

  1. Are recipients of the French national student grant (CROUS) and belong to one of the four highest grant levels (levels 4, 5, 6, or 7); 
  2. Have a disability with a certified degree of invalidity of at least 50%; 
  3. Hold refugee status and/or benefit from international or subsidiary protection, or are displaced persons; 
  4. Have dependent minor children (students who have given birth to a child during the 2026–2027 academic year, as proven by a birth certificate, up to the child’s first birthday); 
  5. Are engaged in employment (students employed, other than occasionally and not by a family member up to and including the second degree, for a period of at least six months within the 12 months preceding the mobility period, in documented employment, self-employment, or professional activity in the public or private sector); 
  6. Are recognised professional athletes (students who are athletes of national interest must present a certificate from the relevant sports federation); 
  7. Are orphans of at least one parent (a student is considered an orphan if their father and/or mother died before the date of submission of the mobility application. This status is recognised provided that the student: (a) is under 26 years of age at the time of application, and/or (b) was financially dependent on the deceased parent at the time of death or is in a similarly economically dependent situation); 
  8. Are children of victims of terrorism or organised crime. 

Supporting documents for Item B will be requested only from successful applicants. 

4. Payment mechanism 

4.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is paid in two instalments: 

4.1.1 The first instalment, equal to 80% of the total estimated scholarship amount, will be paid within 30 days of signing the Mobility Agreement, provided that the student: 

  1. Has submitted a Learning Agreement duly approved and signed by GEM and the host Higher Education Institution; 
  2. Has correctly entered their bank details in the designated system. 

If any of the above conditions are not met, payment of the first instalment will be made within 30 days of their fulfilment. 

4.1.2 The second instalment, representing the remaining 20%, will be paid at the end of the mobility period, subject to verification of: 

  1. Fulfilment of the administrative and procedural obligations set out in this call; 
  2. Successful completion of the authorised mobility period; 
  3. Achievement of learning outcomes consistent with the Learning Agreement; 
  4. Proper administrative completion of the mobility period. 

Failure to comply with any of the above conditions may result in the loss of entitlement to the final payment and may lead to the total or partial recovery of sums already received. 

Acceptance of the mobility period constitutes a formal commitment by the candidate. Consequently, cancellations must be limited to serious and duly documented cases of force majeure. Any cancellation must be communicated in writing to the DIGI-ME Coordinator (digi-me@unipv.it), with GEM Global – DIGI-ME Section (digime.mobility@grenoble-em.com) in copy, adequately justified, and submitted promptly. Cancellation entails the refund of any financial contributions already received. The reason for cancellation and/or failure to communicate it may be considered when assessing eligibility for future GEM international mobility programmes. 

4.2 Tax treatment 

4.2.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is awarded exclusively to support participation in the triple degree mobility programme. The scholarship is intended to contribute to tuition and mobility-related expenses and does not constitute remuneration for employment, services, or research activities. 

4.2.2 Under French tax legislation, grants awarded to support studies and educational mobility are generally not treated as employment income where they are not paid in exchange for work or services. The DIGI-ME scholarship is awarded solely for educational purposes and does not create any employment relationship between GEM and the beneficiary. 

4.2.3 The tax treatment of the scholarship ultimately depends on the individual circumstances of each beneficiary and on the applicable legislation in force at the time of payment. Beneficiaries are solely responsible for determining any personal tax obligations and, where necessary, for making any required declarations to the competent tax authorities. 

4.2.4 GEM does not provide tax advice and accepts no liability for the individual tax treatment of the scholarship. Applicants are encouraged to consult the French tax authorities or a qualified tax adviser if they require guidance regarding their personal tax situation. For more information, please refer to the French tax administration impots.gouv.fr or service-public.fr. 

5. Evaluation process 

Applications must be submitted EXCLUSIVELY through the dedicated form from 18 September 2026 (09:00, Brussels time) to 18 November 2026 (18:00, Brussels time). A complete list of applicants will be compiled, including basic information for statistical and transparency purposes, and may be shared with the European Commission. Applications that pass the eligibility check will undergo an internal evaluation, conducted by a panel of three experts from GEM. For more information on the selection and evaluation process, please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants (Annex 1). The outcome of the call for awarding the DIGI-ME scholarship will be published on the GEM DIGI-ME page. 

6. Eligibility criteria 

The following applicants are eligible: 

6.1 Students regularly enrolled in one of the following DIGI-ME master’s programmes at Grenoble Ecole de Management: 

  1. MSc Managing with Data and Artificial Intelligence; 
  2. MSc in Innovation and Entrepreneurship; 
  3. MSc in Management in International Business; 

Applicants must be: 

  1. Enrolled for the academic year 2026–2027;
  2. Full-time students; 
  3. Not on academic leave. 

6.2 Citizens of the European Union (hereinafter referred to as the EU) or of eligible DEP countries (the full list is available here: list-3rd-country-participation_digital_en.pdf). 

6.3 Proficiency in English is a fundamental requirement, as English is the official language of both the Open Call and the master’s programmes. 

Unless the applicant is a native English speaker, they must provide evidence meeting one of the following minimum requirements: 

  1. TOEFL iBT: 80;

1. Aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships

The aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships (hereinafter referred to as the SCHOLARSHIPS) is to support students in completing their full curriculum through a triple degree programme at the University of Pavia and the University of Vaasa, thereby extending their knowledge and skills in advanced digital technologies (one of the DIGI-ME target areas). 

2. DIGI-ME Scholarships 

The SCHOLARSHIPS are granted by the DIGI-ME project. The DIGI-ME project is co-funded by the European Union under Grant Agreement No. 101123009. Up to EUR 100,000 is available to be distributed through targeted scholarships at Grenoble Ecole de Management (hereinafter referred to as GEM). Through this call, up to ten (10) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their participation in the DIGI-ME path of the triple degree programme with the University of Pavia and the University of Vaasa. 

3. Financial value 

3.1 Scholarships are provided as a lump sum to support students in paying their tuition fees during the triple degree exchange programme. Each selected beneficiary will receive a lump sum for two mobility periods totalling 8 to 10 months, depending on the individual Learning Agreement, in the period from January 2027 to May 2027 at the University of Pavia (Italy) and from January 2028 to May 2028 at the University of Vaasa (Finland). 

The scholarship comprises a minimum of one component (Item A) and a maximum of two components (Items A and B). 

3.1.1 Fixed component 

Item A: Total contribution towards tuition fees: EUR 8,000 (one-time payment). 

3.1.2 Additional component based on special conditions 

Item B: Additional contribution towards tuition fees for participants with fewer opportunities: EUR 2,000 (one-time payment). 

Participants with fewer opportunities are defined as students who, prior to the start of the mobility period, meet one or more of the following criteria: 

  1. Are recipients of the French national student grant (CROUS) and belong to one of the four highest grant levels (levels 4, 5, 6, or 7); 
  2. Have a disability with a certified degree of invalidity of at least 50%; 
  3. Hold refugee status and/or benefit from international or subsidiary protection, or are displaced persons; 
  4. Have dependent minor children (students who have given birth to a child during the 2026–2027 academic year, as proven by a birth certificate, up to the child’s first birthday); 
  5. Are engaged in employment (students employed, other than occasionally and not by a family member up to and including the second degree, for a period of at least six months within the 12 months preceding the mobility period, in documented employment, self-employment, or professional activity in the public or private sector); 
  6. Are recognised professional athletes (students who are athletes of national interest must present a certificate from the relevant sports federation); 
  7. Are orphans of at least one parent (a student is considered an orphan if their father and/or mother died before the date of submission of the mobility application.   8. Are children of victims of terrorism or organised crime. 

Supporting documents for Item B will be requested only from successful applicants. 

4. Payment mechanism 

4.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is paid in two instalments:

4.1.2 The second instalment, representing the remaining 20%, will be paid at the end of the mobility period, subject to verification of: 

  1. Fulfilment of the administrative and procedural obligations set out in this call; 
  2. Successful completion of the authorised mobility period; 
  3. Achievement of learning outcomes consistent with the Learning Agreement; 
  4. Proper administrative completion of the mobility period. 

Failure to comply with any of the above conditions may result in the loss of entitlement to the final payment and may lead to the total or partial recovery of sums already received. 

Acceptance of the mobility period constitutes a formal commitment by the candidate. Consequently, cancellations must be limited to serious and duly documented cases of force majeure. 4.2.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is awarded exclusively to support participation in the triple degree mobility programme. The scholarship is intended to contribute to tuition and mobility-related expenses and does not constitute remuneration for employment, services, or research activities. 

4.2.2 Under French tax legislation, grants awarded to support studies and educational mobility are generally not treated as employment income where they are not paid in exchange for work or services. callTitle: METU Internships Offer
furtherInformation:
INTERNSHIP OPPORTUNITY


TITLE OF INTERNSHIP: Hands-On AI & Data Science Internships

LOCATION: 

Remote (Virtual) or On-Site at Informatics Institute of Middle East Technical University

DURATION: 4 weeks

ELIGIBLE CANDIDATES: Biology, Molecular Biology and Genetics, Engineering, and Biomedical - Bioinformatics Students (BSc/MSc)

OVERVIEW

The Informatics Institute provides a unique research and learning environment across the interdisciplinary fields of medical informatics, bioinformatics, data informatics, and information systems.

We're offering exciting internship opportunities for students passionate about Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science, and Digital Health Technologies. This hands-on experience will deeply immerse you in: 

  1. Nextflow Pipelines: You'll work with NextFlow computational workflows, seamlessly integrated with container technologies like Docker and Singularity, for critical analyses such as differential gene expression and differential ChIP-seq. 
  2. SigProfiler Suite: You'll gain expertise with the powerful SigProfiler tools specialized in cancer genomics, including SigProfilerMatrixGenerator, SigProfilerSimulator, SigProfilerExtractor, SigProfilerAssignment, and SigProfilerTopography. 

This experience will transform your theoretical knowledge into practical, in-demand skills, preparing you for a successful career in data-driven scientific fields. 


DELIVERY MODE & WORK ENVIRONMENT 

  1. Virtual Internships: A cost-effective alternative allowing students to work remotely. 
  2. On-Site Internships: Available in the classroom at the Informatics Institute for students who prefer in-person collaboration. 
  3. Hybrid Approach: Combining remote and on-site work for flexibility. 

Interns will work in small interdisciplinary teams under the guidance of mentors, engaging in collaborative research and development. 

 

WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON 

  1. Building Robust Nextflow Pipelines: Developing and optimizing Nextflow computational workflows that leverage Docker and Singularity container technologies. These pipelines will be crucial for performing advanced analyses like differential gene expression and differential ChIP-seq. 
  2. Mastering the SigProfiler Suite: Becoming proficient with a suite of powerful SigProfiler tools, specifically SigProfilerMatrixGenerator, SigProfilerSimulator, SigProfilerExtractor, SigProfilerAssignment, and SigProfilerTopography. 

TECHNOLOGIES YOU’LL USE  

  1. Python, R 
  2. Nextflow 
  3. SigProfiler suite of tools 

WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU  

  1. Curiosity and willingness to learn 
  2. Python programming knowledge 
  3. Interest in computational biology and bioinformatics 
  4. Teamwork skills 

 


LEARNING OUTCOMES 

Upon completion, interns will: 

✅ Design & Implement Nextflow Pipelines. 

✅ Master Containerization Technologies. 

✅ Ensure Workflow Reproducibility. 

✅ Manage Large-Scale Data. 

✅ Mastering the powerful SigProfiler tools for cancer genomics analysis. 

 

ASSESSMENT & CERTIFICATION 

  1. Completion of assigned tasks and active participation in projects. 
  2. Development of a mini research report or technical presentation at the end of the internship. 
  3. Issuance of an Internship Certificate by the Informatics Institute of Middle East Technical University. 

 

 

APPLICATION PROCESS 

Interested students should submit: 

📌 A short CV highlighting relevant skills and background. 

📌 A brief motivation letter (max. 1 page) explaining their interest in the internship. 

📩 Applications should be sent to: [burcako@metu.edu.tr] with the subject: 

“SUSA Internship Application – [Your Name]” 

For more details, visit contact [burcako@metu.edu.tr].  

This internship offers a unique opportunity to fill the gap between foundational academic knowledge and the practical, industry-ready skills required to excel in the rapidly evolving landscape of data-driven digital health. 

Financial support will be available to facilitate student mobility. SUSA students will have access to internship opportunities offered by both consortium members and affiliated ecosystem partners. The selection criteria for these internships will be developed collaboratively through a co-design process and will incorporate Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) principles, with particular attention to gender and the socio-economic background of applicants.

Student exchanges between Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) will be further supported through a structured and mentored Erasmus+ mobility initiative. To assist students in planning their mobility paths, joint SUSA learning activities will be organized. Additionally, the SUSA Virtual Academy will host a dedicated matchmaking platform, enabling students and teachers to explore internship opportunities and allowing healthcare ecosystem stakeholders to promote openings and connect with emerging talent.

OVERVIEW 

Gnomon Informatics SA, a leading informatics company specializing in digital health solutions, is offering internship opportunities for students interested in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science, and Digital Health Technologies. This internship provides hands-on experience with eHealthPass, a certified patient-centered platform for remote patient monitoring, which includes a mobile app for patients and a web application for healthcare professionals. eHealthPass is a solution for remote care, virtual care and hospital at home, as well as communication and patient empowerment tool, putting patient in the middle and allowing patient to become stakeholder in own care instead of being mere subject of care. Behind eHealthPass there is also the eHealthPass.CDR, a platform providing and enabling HIE (Health Information Exchange) – complete lifecycle management of structured and unstructured clinical documents and clinical data, and their secure sharing/exchange.  

Interns will contribute to AI development, data quality enhancement, and predictive analytics in healthcare, gaining invaluable experience in a multidisciplinary setting. 

 

INTERNSHIP TRACKS 

1. Medical Students – AI and Digital Health Applications 

  1. Assisting in training AI models by feeding them with structured and unstructured medical data. 
  2. Understanding and improving AI-assisted decision support tools for clinical applications. 
  3. Exploring ways to generate customized outcomes and predictions for individual patients. 
  4. Medical file structures and content (questionnaires, educational and other materials) 
  5. Usability of the product 

2. Engineering & Data Science Students – Data & AI Optimization 

  1. Contributing to data quality assessment and enhancing data mesh architecture. 
  2. Developing and testing AI tools for predictive analytics and patient monitoring. 
  3. Exploring interoperability challenges in digital health using HL7 FHIR and other HL7 standards (HL7v2 messages, HL7 CDA). 
  4. Assisting in data visualization techniques to support decision-making for healthcare providers (UX/UI for HealthTech) 

3. Bioinformatics/ Biomedical Students – Clinical Data  

  1. Clinical data model and governance 
  2. Terminology management 
  3. GDPR & EHDS issues 
  4. eHealthPass use cases validation & scenarios 

 

DELIVERY MODE & WORK ENVIRONMENT 

  1. Virtual Internships: A cost-effective alternative allowing students to work remotely while accessing Gnomon’s digital infrastructure. 
  2. On-Site Internships: Available at our company headquarters for students who prefer in-person collaboration. 
  3. Hybrid Approach: Combining remote and on-site work for flexibility. 

Interns will work in small interdisciplinary teams under the guidance of mentors and domain experts, engaging in collaborative research and development. 

WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON 

  1. Healthcare Interoperability: Learn and apply standards like FHIR, HL7, and IHE XDS. 
  2. Artificial Intelligence: Participate in AI-powered solutions for clinical decision support, health record processing, and document classification. 
  3. Software Development: Collaborate in real projects, using Java, Spring Boot, Python, APIs, and cloud platforms (Azure, AWS). 
  4. Medical Data Processing: Work with EHR systems, patient summaries, and secure document exchanges 
  5. R&D Projects: Contribute to European Research Projects and pilot implementations in real healthcare settings. 

TECHNOLOGIES YOU’LL USE  

  1. Java/ Spring Boot/ Python 
  2. FHIR/ HL7/ IHE 
  3. Azure/ AWS/ Docker/ Kubernetes 
  4. AI Models/ Prompt Engineering/ LLMs  

WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU   

  1. Curiosity and willingness to learn 
  2. Basic programming knowledge (preferably Jana or Python) 
  3. Interest in healthcare or AI 
  4. Teamwork skills  

 

LEARNING OUTCOMES 

Upon completion, interns will: 

✅ Gain practical experience in digital health platforms and AI integration. 

✅ Understand data governance, privacy regulations (GDPR), and interoperability. 

✅ Develop hands-on skills in data science, machine learning, and healthcare informatics. 

✅ Enhance problem-solving and critical thinking abilities in a real-world healthcare environment. 

 

ASSESSMENT & CERTIFICATION 

  1. Completion of assigned tasks and active participation in projects. 
  2. Development of a mini research report or technical presentation at the end of the internship. 
  3. Issuance of an Internship Certificate by Gnomon Informatics SA, potentially co-branded with academic institutions. 

 

APPLICATION PROCESS 

Interested students should submit: 

📌 A short CV highlighting relevant skills and background. 

📌 A brief motivation letter (max. 1 page) explaining their interest in the internship and preferred track (Medical or Engineering). 

📩 Applications should be sent to: a.karabatea@gnomon.com.gr with the subject: 

“Digital Health Internship Application – [Your Name]” 

For more details, visit contact a.karabatea@gnomon.com.gr . 

This internship offers a unique opportunity to fill the gap between foundational academic knowledge and the practical, industry-ready skills required to excel in the rapidly evolving landscape of data-driven digital health. 

Financial support will be available to facilitate student mobility. SUSA students will have access to internship opportunities offered by both consortium members and affiliated ecosystem partners. The selection criteria for these internships will be developed collaboratively through a co-design process and will incorporate Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) principles, with particular attention to gender and the socio-economic background of applicants.

Student exchanges between Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) will be further supported through a structured and mentored Erasmus+ mobility initiative. To assist students in planning their mobility paths, joint SUSA learning activities will be organized. Additionally, the SUSA Virtual Academy will host a dedicated matchmaking platform, enabling students and teachers to explore internship opportunities and allowing healthcare ecosystem stakeholders to promote openings and connect with emerging talent.

results.summary: InnoEnergy Masters+ Scholarship — MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI (AI4GreenDeal)
results.content: InnoEnergy Masters+ Scholarship — MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI (AI4GreenDeal)

beneficiaryAdministration:
The AI4GreenDeal project delivers a 120-ECTS Master’s double-degree programme combining energy-domain knowledge with data and AI skills and with innovation and entrepreneurship training, complemented by flexible, stackable self-standing modules. Through this call, the consortium offers to students (Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP)) in the form of full or partial scholarships to attract highly qualified candidates and to widen access to the programme, in line with the project’s target of at least 30% participation from women and/or individuals from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

Two scholarship schemes are offered under this call:

  1. Energy Impact Scholarships — awarded to applicants who demonstrate strong academic preparation and potential to contribute to the energy transition.
  2. Diversity, Entrepreneurship and Digital Champions (DED) Scholarships — awarded across three strands (DEI; Entrepreneurship; Digital Champions) to promote diversity and recognise entrepreneurial or digital-innovation excellence.

Applications are submitted through the InnoEnergy Masters+ online application tool within the published application window: 

https://apply.innoenergy.com/courses/course/55-masters-advanced-energy-systems-and-ai.

The MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI operates a rolling intake with five application rounds between 21 September 2026 and 30 May 2027; scholarship decisions are taken after each round within the overall framework and budget communicated for the intake.

No separate scholarship application is required: every applicant admitted to the programme is automatically considered for an Energy Impact Scholarship and admitted applicants who submit a 1–2 minute motivation video and pay the registration fee may in addition be considered for a DED Scholarship.

Each application is assessed in three stages. The Admissions Office first verifies document validity, general admissibility, recipient eligibility, and exclusion criteria. The Programme Steering Committee — composed of academic representatives of the partner universities acting as independent experts — then confirms programme-specific eligibility, evaluates, and ranks eligible applicants against the published award criteria.( https://ai4greendeal.com/content/uploads/2026/09/AI4GreenDeal_Indicative_Evaluation_Rubrics_070926.pdf ) The programme-independent DED Selection Committee additionally evaluates DED applicants.

Before scoring, every evaluator signs a declaration of confidentiality and absence of conflict of interest. Committee decisions require a quorum, and each round is closed with a signed selection-confirmation report. Scholarship awards are approved by the FSTP Management Office and communicated by official acceptance letter issued by the Admissions Office and signed by the Programme Director. Applicants must confirm participation within five working days of the acceptance letter.

Applicants may appeal decisions on general admissibility or programme-specific eligibility within the period stated in the rejection communication. Scholarship and ranking outcomes are not subject to academic appeal but may be reviewed for procedural compliance.

In case students decline their offer for a scholarship or scholarship funding cannot be allocated because of applicants not fulfilling the minimum thresholds, the remaining budget will move to the next available cut-off moment. If after the fifth cut-off moment, budget is remaining, it may be allocated to students from previous rounds in the order of scoring (highest to lowest).

Eligible countries

Scholarship recipients must be natural persons holding the nationality of one of the DEP eligible countries, which for the intake 2027 is the list of countries below Should the list of DEP eligible countries change, then other nationalities may become eligible.

EU Member States and Associated Digital Europe Programme (DEP) Countries: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Switzerland.

Other Eligible Non-EU Countries: Albania, Algeria, Armenia, Argentina, Australia, Azerbaijan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Canada, Egypt, Georgia, India, Israel, Japan, Jordan, Kosovo, Lebanon, Libya, Mexico, Moldova, Montenegro, Morocco, North Macedonia, Palestine, Serbia, Singapore, South Korea, Syria, Taiwan, Tunisia, Ukraine, United States.

Common eligibility and exclusion grounds

The conditions in this section apply to both the Energy Impact Scholarships and the DED Scholarships. Scheme-specific eligibility conditions are set out under each scholarship.

Common eligibility conditions

To be eligible for a scholarship under this call, an applicant must:

  1. hold the nationality of one of the countries listed in eligible countries.
  2. be admitted to the MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI; and
  3. accept the InnoEnergy Student Code of Conduct.

Exclusion grounds

An applicant is excluded from consideration for any scholarship under this call, and any scholarship already awarded may be withdrawn, where the applicant:

  1. has previously received an InnoEnergy scholarship.
  2. has submitted false or materially misleading information at any point in the application process.
  3. is receiving other EU funding covering the same participation costs (no double funding); or
  4. is subject to EU restrictive measures.

The Admissions Office verifies these conditions on the basis of documentary evidence and records the outcome in the application tool. Applicants who do not meet the common eligibility conditions or who fall under an exclusion ground are excluded from scholarship support, with the reason recorded.

1. Energy Impact Scholarships

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. About UPRAISE

UPRAISE – Virtual Worlds Innovation Masters: Shaping Future Digital Skills Europe is implemented under the Digital Europe Programme and coordinated by the University of Bologna. The project aims to strengthen advanced digital skills in Europe through innovative and interdisciplinary education and training related to Virtual Worlds and their applications in different economic and societal domains. Within UPRAISE, the University of Napoli Federico II contributes to the Public Administration application area, focusing on the organizational, managerial and institutional implications of digital transformation and emerging digital technologies in the public sector.

2. Purpose of the Call

The University of Napoli Federico II launches this Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) call within Task T5.2 – “Mobility, mentorship and (non-)financial support for students” of the UPRAISE project. The call aims to facilitate access to advanced education and training opportunities connected with UPRAISE and to reduce financial and socio-economic barriers to participation.

For Cycle 1, UNINA proposes to award financial support in the form of Tuition and Enrolment Fee Waivers to eligible students admitted to the educational pathway described in Section 3.

3. Educational pathway covered by the Call

For Cycle 1, the UNINA UPRAISE educational pathway will be developed in connection with the following postgraduate programmes offered by the Department of Economics, Management, Institutions (DEMI) for academic year 2025/2026:

-Master in Public Managerial Practice (Master in Pratica Manageriale Pubblica); -Master in Digital Transformation of Public Administration (Master in Trasformazione Digitale della Pubblica Amministrazione).

FSTP beneficiaries will also be required to participate in a dedicated UPRAISE specialized learning activity/self-standing module in the Public Administration area, entitled: “Digital Transformation, Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Worlds for Public Administration”.

The UPRAISE specialised learning activity will consist of 24 hours of online learning and will complement the educational activities of the relevant Master programme. It will focus on the application and organisational implications of advanced digital technologies in Public Administration, with particular reference to: Artificial Intelligence and data-driven public services; Virtual Worlds, immersive technologies and digital twins; organizational and managerial implications of emerging technologies; innovation in public services.

The activity is intended to enable participants to understand and critically assess the opportunities, organisational implications and governance challenges associated with the adoption of these technologies in the public sector, and to apply the knowledge acquired to relevant Public Administration contexts.

Completion of the UPRAISE specialised learning activity requires attendance of at least 70% of the scheduled activities and a positive final assessment. Participants who successfully complete the activity will receive a UPRAISE Certificate of Completion. For cycle 1 this activity does not award ECTS credits.

Participation in and successful completion of the UPRAISE specialised learning activity are mandatory conditions for FSTP beneficiaries and for maintaining the financial support awarded under this Call.

4. Financial support available

For Cycle 1, the UNINA allocation is:

• maximum number of beneficiaries: 4;

•      maximum FSTP support per beneficiary: EUR 5,000;

•      maximum total Cycle 1 allocation: EUR 20,000.

The support will take the form of a full or partial Tuition and Enrolment Fee Waiver. The maximum amount of support will depend on the tuition fee applicable to the selected programme: Master in Public Managerial Practice: tuition fee EUR 4,000; maximum FSTP support EUR 4,000; Master in Digital Transformation of Public Administration: tuition fee EUR 10,000; maximum FSTP support EUR 5,000. In all cases, the amount awarded shall comply with the prohibition of double funding.

5. Eligible applicants

Applicants must:

·       meet the academic entry requirements of the relevant programme;

·       be formally admitted to or enrolled in the programmes identified in Section 3;

·       undertake the associated UPRAISE specialized learning activity/self-standing module;

·       satisfy the nationality/country eligibility conditions applicable under the UPRAISE Grant Agreement and Digital Europe Programme;

·       comply with the applicable administrative requirements of the University of Napoli Federico II;

·       not receive other EU financial support covering the same tuition/enrolment costs;

·       provide the documents and declarations required under this call.

Admission to the Master programme and selection for FSTP financial support are separate procedures. Admission to the Master does not automatically entitle an applicant to FSTP support.

6. Inclusion, widening participation and financial need

In accordance with the UPRAISE objectives and FSTP framework, the selection and determination of financial support shall take account, through transparent criteria, of financial need, socio-economic circumstances, geographical/widening considerations, diversity and inclusion, as applicable. Applicants may voluntarily provide information relevant to these criteria, including socio-economic circumstances, disability or other conditions relevant to widening participation. Such information will be processed in accordance with applicable data protection rules. The specific scoring mechanism is set out in Section 11. 

7. Language requirements

Applicants must demonstrate an adequate level of proficiency in the language of instruction of the selected programme and associated UPRAISE learning activities, in accordance with the requirements established by UNINA. Where applicable, some UPRAISE activities, learning materials, seminars or international sessions may be delivered in English. 

8. Application procedure

Applications shall be submitted electronically through the procedure specified by UNINA. The call shall remain open for at least two months. The published call will specify the opening and closing dates, submission platform and contacts for administrative and technical enquiries. Applications submitted after the deadline or through channels other than those indicated in the call will not be considered.

9. Required documents

In line with the FSTP Guidelines, applicants should provide, as a minimum:

1.     Transcript of Records or equivalent academic documentation;

2.     Curriculum Vitae, maximum 3 pages, without photograph, including academic history, relevant professional experience, skills and achievements;

3.     Personal Statement/Motivation Letter, maximum 3 pages, addressing motivation for participation, relevance to UPRAISE and the proposed educational pathway, and expected academic/professional impact;

4.     copy of a valid passport or identity document;

5.     any additional documents required by UNINA to verify eligibility.

Applicants may be required to provide a declaration concerning other financial support and compliance with the applicable double-funding rules. Where relevant to the published financial-need, widening or inclusion criteria, applicants may voluntarily provide the information and supporting documentation expressly identified in the final call. UNINA will not request sensitive personal data beyond what is necessary and legally permissible for the implementation of the published criteria.

10. Eligibility check

Following the deadline, UNINA will conduct an eligibility check. Only applications satisfying the eligibility requirements, submitted on time and accompanied by the mandatory documentation will proceed to evaluation.

11. Evaluation and selection criteria

Eligible applications will be evaluated by a Selection Committee appointed by UNINA on the basis of clear, objective and transparent criteria, in accordance with Section 5.3 of the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines. Applications will be assessed on a maximum score of 100 points according to the following criteria

Criterion

Description

Weight

Academic background

Academic and Professional Background – academic records, previous qualifications, relevant professional experience and achievements, and overall preparedness for the proposed advanced digital skills learning pathway.

65 points

Motivation and proposed activity

Motivation and Expected Contribution – motivation to participate in the programme, interest in the thematic areas addressed by UPRAISE, expected contribution to the applicant’s professional and/or academic development, and potential contribution to the broader objectives and impact of the project

25 points

Curriculum Vitae

Additional Academic and Non-Academic Experience – additional relevant academic, professional and non-academic experience, skills and achievements documented in the Curriculum Vitae.

10 points



100 points

In accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines, the quality and relevance of the proposed participation in relation to the applicant’s educational and professional objectives will be considered within the above assessment criteria. Applicants must demonstrate an adequate level of proficiency in the language of instruction of the selected programme, in accordance with the requirements specified by UNINA. Diversity, equity, inclusion and widening participation considerations will be taken into account in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines. In the case of equal or comparable evaluation results, preference may be given to applicants from underrepresented groups, subject to applicable legal and institutional rules.

Applicants achieving an overall score of at least 70/100 may be considered for funding, subject to compliance with all eligibility requirements and availability of financial resources.

12. Selection committee

The Selection Committee will be appointed in accordance with UNINA rules. Its members shall act independently and impartially and comply with applicable confidentiality and conflict-of-interest requirements. The Committee will assess eligible applications against the published criteria, assign scores and establish the ranking.

13. Ranking, reserve list and award decision

Financial support will be awarded, subject to availability of funds, to the highest-ranked eligible applicants meeting the minimum threshold. A maximum of four beneficiaries will be funded under this Cycle 1 call. Eligible applicants above the threshold but not funded may be placed on a reserve list in ranking order. Where fewer than four applicants satisfy the eligibility and quality requirements, fewer than four applicants may be awarded financial support under this Call. If a selected applicant withdraws, declines the award, fails to accept it within the prescribed deadline or loses eligibility, UNINA may offer the support to the next eligible applicant on the reserve list.

14. Communication and acceptance of results

Applicants will be informed of the outcome of the selection procedure in accordance with the FSTP Guidelines. Successful applicants will receive information concerning the financial support awarded and the procedures for its acceptance. Applicants placed on the reserve list and applicants whose applications are declared ineligible or unsuccessful will be informed in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines.

15. Conditions for maintaining the support

Beneficiaries must maintain eligibility and participation in the relevant educational pathway, successfully complete the associated UPRAISE specialised learning activity in accordance with the attendance and assessment requirements set out in Section 3, comply with applicable academic and administrative requirements, provide information required for project monitoring and promptly communicate changes affecting eligibility or funding. Beneficiaries shall comply with the participation and reporting obligations established by the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines and by the relevant UNINA educational programme.

16. Fee waiver and administrative arrangements

The FSTP support under this Call is intended to cover tuition/enrolment fees through a full or partial fee waiver. No part of the financial support, including any difference between the applicable tuition/enrolment fee waiver and the maximum FSTP support of EUR 5,000 per beneficiary, will be paid directly to beneficiaries or provided in another form. The maximum support is EUR 4,000 for beneficiaries enrolled in the Master in Public Managerial Practice and EUR 5,000 for beneficiaries enrolled in the Master in Digital Transformation of Public Administration. The amount of the benefit will be individually recorded. The administrative and accounting mechanism will comply with UNINA procedures and the UPRAISE Grant Agreement.

17. Double funding

Financial support awarded under this Call shall comply with the applicable rules on double funding, in accordance with the UPRAISE Grant Agreement and FSTP Guidelines.

18. Monitoring, records and audits

UNINA will retain the documentation required to ensure an adequate audit trail for publication, applications, eligibility checks, evaluation, selection, award and implementation. 

19. Redress procedure

A redress procedure will be provided in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines and the applicable UNINA procedures.

20. Data protection 

Personal data submitted in connection with this Call will be processed in accordance with the applicable data protection legislation and the relevant University of Napoli Federico II privacy notice.

21. Publication and visibility

Following the required review and confirmation procedure, the call will be published simultaneously through the channels required by the UPRAISE/HaDEA implementation arrangements, including the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, the Digital Skills and Jobs Platform (DSJP), the UPRAISE project website and the institutional website of the University of Napoli Federico II. The call will remain open for at least two months. The English version will be the reference version; an Italian version may also be made available.

22. Disclaimer

This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by UPRAISE. Any financial support awarded under this call will be granted directly by UPRAISE to the successful applicants, in its own name and under its sole responsibility. UPRAISE's own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants that will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim to increase the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of UPRAISE.
