The University of Napoli Federico II launches this Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) call within Task T5.2 – “Mobility, mentorship and (non-)financial support for students” of the UPRAISE project. The call aims to facilitate access to advanced education and training opportunities connected with UPRAISE and to reduce financial and socio-economic barriers to participation.

For Cycle 1, UNINA proposes to award financial support in the form of Tuition and Enrolment Fee Waivers to eligible students admitted to the educational pathway described in Section 3.

3. Educational pathway covered by the Call

For Cycle 1, the UNINA UPRAISE educational pathway will be developed in connection with the following postgraduate programmes offered by the Department of Economics, Management, Institutions (DEMI) for academic year 2025/2026:

-Master in Public Managerial Practice (Master in Pratica Manageriale Pubblica); -Master in Digital Transformation of Public Administration (Master in Trasformazione Digitale della Pubblica Amministrazione).

FSTP beneficiaries will also be required to participate in a dedicated UPRAISE specialized learning activity/self-standing module in the Public Administration area, entitled: “Digital Transformation, Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Worlds for Public Administration”.

The UPRAISE specialised learning activity will consist of 24 hours of online learning and will complement the educational activities of the relevant Master programme. It will focus on the application and organisational implications of advanced digital technologies in Public Administration, with particular reference to: Artificial Intelligence and data-driven public services; Virtual Worlds, immersive technologies and digital twins; organizational and managerial implications of emerging technologies; innovation in public services.

The activity is intended to enable participants to understand and critically assess the opportunities, organisational implications and governance challenges associated with the adoption of these technologies in the public sector, and to apply the knowledge acquired to relevant Public Administration contexts.

Completion of the UPRAISE specialised learning activity requires attendance of at least 70% of the scheduled activities and a positive final assessment. Participants who successfully complete the activity will receive a UPRAISE Certificate of Completion. For cycle 1 this activity does not award ECTS credits.

Participation in and successful completion of the UPRAISE specialised learning activity are mandatory conditions for FSTP beneficiaries and for maintaining the financial support awarded under this Call.

4. Financial support available

For Cycle 1, the UNINA allocation is:

• maximum number of beneficiaries: 4;

•      maximum FSTP support per beneficiary: EUR 5,000;

•      maximum total Cycle 1 allocation: EUR 20,000.

The support will take the form of a full or partial Tuition and Enrolment Fee Waiver. The maximum amount of support will depend on the tuition fee applicable to the selected programme: Master in Public Managerial Practice: tuition fee EUR 4,000; maximum FSTP support EUR 4,000; Master in Digital Transformation of Public Administration: tuition fee EUR 10,000; maximum FSTP support EUR 5,000. In all cases, the amount awarded shall comply with the prohibition of double funding.

5. Eligible applicants

Applicants must:

·       meet the academic entry requirements of the relevant programme;

·       be formally admitted to or enrolled in the programmes identified in Section 3;

·       undertake the associated UPRAISE specialized learning activity/self-standing module;

·       satisfy the nationality/country eligibility conditions applicable under the UPRAISE Grant Agreement and Digital Europe Programme;

·       comply with the applicable administrative requirements of the University of Napoli Federico II;

·       not receive other EU financial support covering the same tuition/enrolment costs;

·       provide the documents and declarations required under this call.

Admission to the Master programme and selection for FSTP financial support are separate procedures. Admission to the Master does not automatically entitle an applicant to FSTP support.

6. Inclusion, widening participation and financial need

In accordance with the UPRAISE objectives and FSTP framework, the selection and determination of financial support shall take account, through transparent criteria, of financial need, socio-economic circumstances, geographical/widening considerations, diversity and inclusion, as applicable. Applicants may voluntarily provide information relevant to these criteria, including socio-economic circumstances, disability or other conditions relevant to widening participation. Such information will be processed in accordance with applicable data protection rules. The specific scoring mechanism is set out in Section 11. 

7. Language requirements

Applicants must demonstrate an adequate level of proficiency in the language of instruction of the selected programme and associated UPRAISE learning activities, in accordance with the requirements established by UNINA. Where applicable, some UPRAISE activities, learning materials, seminars or international sessions may be delivered in English. 

8. Application procedure

Applications shall be submitted electronically through the procedure specified by UNINA. The call shall remain open for at least two months. The published call will specify the opening and closing dates, submission platform and contacts for administrative and technical enquiries. Applications submitted after the deadline or through channels other than those indicated in the call will not be considered.

9. Required documents

In line with the FSTP Guidelines, applicants should provide, as a minimum:

1.     Transcript of Records or equivalent academic documentation;

2.     Curriculum Vitae, maximum 3 pages, without photograph, including academic history, relevant professional experience, skills and achievements;

3.     Personal Statement/Motivation Letter, maximum 3 pages, addressing motivation for participation, relevance to UPRAISE and the proposed educational pathway, and expected academic/professional impact;

4.     copy of a valid passport or identity document;

5.     any additional documents required by UNINA to verify eligibility.

Applicants may be required to provide a declaration concerning other financial support and compliance with the applicable double-funding rules. Where relevant to the published financial-need, widening or inclusion criteria, applicants may voluntarily provide the information and supporting documentation expressly identified in the final call. UNINA will not request sensitive personal data beyond what is necessary and legally permissible for the implementation of the published criteria.

10. Eligibility check

Following the deadline, UNINA will conduct an eligibility check. Only applications satisfying the eligibility requirements, submitted on time and accompanied by the mandatory documentation will proceed to evaluation.

11. Evaluation and selection criteria

Eligible applications will be evaluated by a Selection Committee appointed by UNINA on the basis of clear, objective and transparent criteria, in accordance with Section 5.3 of the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines. Applications will be assessed on a maximum score of 100 points according to the following criteria

Criterion

Academic background

In accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines, the quality and relevance of the proposed participation in relation to the applicant’s educational and professional objectives will be considered within the above assessment criteria. Applicants must demonstrate an adequate level of proficiency in the language of instruction of the selected programme, in accordance with the requirements specified by UNINA. Diversity, equity, inclusion and widening participation considerations will be taken into account in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines. In the case of equal or comparable evaluation results, preference may be given to applicants from underrepresented groups, subject to applicable legal and institutional rules.

Applicants achieving an overall score of at least 70/100 may be considered for funding, subject to compliance with all eligibility requirements and availability of financial resources.

12. Selection committee

The Selection Committee will be appointed in accordance with UNINA rules. Its members shall act independently and impartially and comply with applicable confidentiality and conflict-of-interest requirements. The Committee will assess eligible applications against the published criteria, assign scores and establish the ranking.

13. Ranking, reserve list and award decision

Financial support will be awarded, subject to availability of funds, to the highest-ranked eligible applicants meeting the minimum threshold. A maximum of four beneficiaries will be funded under this Cycle 1 call. Eligible applicants above the threshold but not funded may be placed on a reserve list in ranking order. Where fewer than four applicants satisfy the eligibility and quality requirements, fewer than four applicants may be awarded financial support under this Call. If a selected applicant withdraws, declines the award, fails to accept it within the prescribed deadline or loses eligibility, UNINA may offer the support to the next eligible applicant on the reserve list.

14. Communication and acceptance of results

Applicants will be informed of the outcome of the selection procedure in accordance with the FSTP Guidelines. Successful applicants will receive information concerning the financial support awarded and the procedures for its acceptance. Applicants placed on the reserve list and applicants whose applications are declared ineligible or unsuccessful will be informed in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines.

15. Conditions for maintaining the support

Beneficiaries must maintain eligibility and participation in the relevant educational pathway, successfully complete the associated UPRAISE specialised learning activity in accordance with the attendance and assessment requirements set out in Section 3, comply with applicable academic and administrative requirements, provide information required for project monitoring and promptly communicate changes affecting eligibility or funding. Beneficiaries shall comply with the participation and reporting obligations established by the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines and by the relevant UNINA educational programme.

16. Fee waiver and administrative arrangements

The FSTP support under this Call is intended to cover tuition/enrolment fees through a full or partial fee waiver. No part of the financial support, including any difference between the applicable tuition/enrolment fee waiver and the maximum FSTP support of EUR 5,000 per beneficiary, will be paid directly to beneficiaries or provided in another form. The maximum support is EUR 4,000 for beneficiaries enrolled in the Master in Public Managerial Practice and EUR 5,000 for beneficiaries enrolled in the Master in Digital Transformation of Public Administration. The amount of the benefit will be individually recorded. The administrative and accounting mechanism will comply with UNINA procedures and the UPRAISE Grant Agreement.

17. Double funding

Financial support awarded under this Call shall comply with the applicable rules on double funding, in accordance with the UPRAISE Grant Agreement and FSTP Guidelines.

18. Monitoring, records and audits

UNINA will retain the documentation required to ensure an adequate audit trail for publication, applications, eligibility checks, evaluation, selection, award and implementation. 

19. Redress procedure

A redress procedure will be provided in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines and the applicable UNINA procedures.

20. Data protection 

Personal data submitted in connection with this Call will be processed in accordance with the applicable data protection legislation and the relevant University of Napoli Federico II privacy notice.

21. Publication and visibility

Following the required review and confirmation procedure, the call will be published simultaneously through the channels required by the UPRAISE/HaDEA implementation arrangements, including the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, the Digital Skills and Jobs Platform (DSJP), the UPRAISE project website and the institutional website of the University of Napoli Federico II. The call will remain open for at least two months. The English version will be the reference version; an Italian version may also be made available.

22. Disclaimer

This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by UPRAISE. Any financial support awarded under this call will be granted directly by UPRAISE to the successful applicants, in its own name and under its sole responsibility. UPRAISE's own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants that will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim to increase the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of UPRAISE.

furtherInformation:
Eligible applicants

  1. Be formally enrolled at the University of Patras in a doctoral, postgraduate or undergraduate program appropriate to the selected mobility stream.
  2. Meet the academic and administrative requirements of the proposed host institution, program, summer/winter school, internship or learning activity.
  3. Have an academic profile and proposed activity aligned with UPRAISE themes, such as Virtual Worlds, XR, AI, digital twins, advanced digital innovation, or relevant applications in healthcare, education and creativity, and food.
  4. Have adequate command of English, normally at least B2 level, or the language required by the host activity.
  5. Hold the nationality of an EU Member State or another country eligible under the Digital Europe Program, in accordance with the applicable call rules.
  6. Be able to complete the proposed activity within the eligibility period established in the award documentation.


Eligible activities and costs

Financial support may cover only the cost categories specified below and directly related to the approved mobility activity:

  1. Enrolment or participation fees for an eligible program, module, summer/winter school or other approved learning activity.
  2. Travel and accommodation costs.
  3. Living expenses and subsistence during the approved mobility period, including local transport where permitted by institutional rules.

Double funding of the same expense is strictly prohibited. The grant may be combined with another compatible source, such as Erasmus+, only where the funding sources cover different eligible costs and all applicable institutional rules are respected.


Inclusion and prioritisation

The prioritisation categories are applied only after eligibility and academic qualification have been established. They are not mutually exclusive and will support a balanced cohort while preserving merit-based selection. .

  1. Women and other genders underrepresented in ICT-related fields.
  2. Applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds or experiencing significant financial hardship.
  3. Applicants with disabilities and applicants belonging to minority, migrant, refugee or other vulnerable groups.
  4. Applicants from countries or regions with lower advanced digital skills capacity.
  5. Applicants who belong to more than one priority category or who contribute to the overall balance of the selected cohort.

Information relating to priority categories is voluntary, confidential and processed only where necessary under applicable data protection rules. Applicants who wish to be considered under a priority category may provide only the minimum information needed to establish that category: optional gender self-identification; a brief statement of low socio-economic background or significant financial hardship, with income-related or financial-aid evidence where available and permitted under University procedures; a self-declaration that disability, minority, migrant, refugee or other vulnerable-group status applies, with non-diagnostic official confirmation only where strictly necessary; and country or region of residence, origin or prior study for geographical widening. Applicants may also indicate that more than one priority category applies. Applicants are not required to disclose medical diagnoses, detailed health information, ethnicity, religion or other sensitive details beyond what is necessary to establish the claimed category. Where official evidence is unavailable or requesting it would be inappropriate, self-declarations may be accepted in accordance with University procedures and applicable data protection rules. If two or more applicants have the same final score, the Selection Committee may use the above factors, financial need and the overall cohort balance as tie-breakers and must document the rationale.


Award, payment and obligations

  1. All applicants will be informed of the outcome. Successful applicants must accept the award within the period stated in the notification.
  2. Before payment, selected applicants may be required to sign a grant agreement, learning agreement, declaration of honour, double-funding declaration and other University of Patras documents.
  3. Recipients must implement the approved activity, provide evidence of participation and eligible expenditure where requested, and cooperate with monitoring, reporting, audits and checks.
  4. Withdrawal or cancellation must be communicated promptly in writing. Financial support already received may have to be reimbursed when the activity is not implemented or eligibility conditions are not fulfilled.
  5. The selected activity should be academically recognised through ECTS or another appropriate certification where applicable, according to the rules of the University of Patras and the host institution.


Redress procedure

Applicants may request a review only in relation to an alleged procedural or administrative error affecting the evaluation. A redress request may not challenge the academic judgement of evaluators unless a procedural irregularity may have influenced the result. Requests must be submitted to dtsolis@upatras.gr within 10 calendar days of notification.


Data protection and confidentiality

The University of Patras acts as Data Controller for personal data processed in connection with this call. Personal data will be used only for application management, evaluation, award administration, project monitoring, reporting, audit and compliance purposes under Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and applicable national legislation. Applicants will receive or be directed to the relevant University of Patras privacy notice before submission.


Disclaimer

This call, as well as the financial support that will be provided through it, is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by UPRAISE. Any financial support awarded under this call will be granted directly by UPRAISE to the successful applicants, in its own name and under its sole responsibility. UPRAISE's responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants. Publication of this call on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is solely for information purposes and to increase visibility. Such publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any waiver of UPRAISE's responsibility.

Applicants may also indicate that more than one priority category applies. Applicants are not required to disclose medical diagnoses, detailed health information, ethnicity, religion or other sensitive details beyond what is necessary to establish the claimed category. Where official evidence is unavailable or requesting it would be inappropriate, self-declarations may be accepted in accordance with University procedures and applicable data protection rules. If two or more applicants have the same final score, the Selection Committee may use the above factors, financial need and the overall cohort balance as tie-breakers and must document the rationale.

Award, payment and obligations

  1. All applicants will be informed of the outcome. Successful applicants must accept the award within the period stated in the notification.
  2. Before payment, selected applicants may be required to sign a grant agreement, learning agreement, declaration of honour, double-funding declaration and other University of Patras documents.
  3. Recipients must implement the approved activity, provide evidence of participation and eligible expenditure where requested, and cooperate with monitoring, reporting, audits and checks.

Applicants may request a review only in relation to an alleged procedural or administrative error affecting the evaluation. Personal data will be used only for application management, evaluation, award administration, project monitoring, reporting, audit and compliance purposes under Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and applicable national legislation. Applicants will receive or be directed to the relevant University of Patras privacy notice before submission.

results.content: LLM-BRIDGE – Venture Incubation Programme - Open Call for Incubators – 2nd Call

beneficiaryAdministration:
Proposal submission:

All proposals shall be submitted at: https://share.hsforms.com/133VDDomZReqeyGTex0VYRwf4os

Proposal template and supporting documents:

The proposal template and supporting documents are available at: https://www.llm-bridge.eu/open-calls-2/

Evaluation process:

Eligible proposals will be evaluated by independent external experts, appointed by the LLM-BRIDGE Consortium, to ensure objectivity and impartiality.

Each proposal will be assessed by at least two experts using the criteria and scoring system defined in the Evaluation Criteria.

Applicants will be notified of the evaluation results within four weeks after completion of the panel ranking.

Each applicant will receive an Evaluation Summary Report (ESR) containing individual scores, comments, and the final consensus assessment.

The successful applicant will be invited to sign a Financial Support Agreement with 28DIGITAL on behalf of the LLM-BRIDGE Consortium.

Evaluation criteria:

The evaluation is based on the following criteria, each with a maximum score and a minimum threshold:

Relevance (maximum score: 10; threshold: 6): Assessment of how well the proposal aligns with the objectives of LLM-BRIDGE, including its capacity to support early-stage Generative AI startups and contribute to European GenAI strategic goals.

Track record (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Evaluation of the applicant’s proven experience in incubating and scaling AI or deep-tech ventures, with demonstrated results in terms of startup growth and innovation.

Networks and access (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Consideration of the ability to provide startups with access to mentors, investors, and strategic industry partners that can strengthen their market positioning and growth potential.

Adaptability (maximum score: 6; threshold: 4): Evidence of flexibility and capacity to respond to emerging technological and market needs, particularly in the rapidly evolving Generative AI sector.

Monitoring framework (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Quality and clarity of the proposed processes and documentation for monitoring and reporting, including well-defined metrics to track startup progress and overall programme performance.

Cost effectiveness (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Adequacy and justification of the proposed budget, demonstrating efficient use of resources and value for money.

Each criterion is scored from 0 up to its maximum (10, 8, 6 or 5). Proposals are evaluated according to six qualitative levels.

Not addressed (score 0 in all scales): The proposal fails to address the criterion or cannot be assessed.

Poor (score 1–2 out of 10, 1–2 out of 8, or 1 out of 5/6): The proposal shows serious weaknesses or lacks the required level of detail.

Fair (score 3–4 out of 10, 3–4 out of 8, or 2 out of 5/6): Some strengths are present, but significant weaknesses remain.

Good – threshold level (score 5–6 out of 10, 5 out of 8, or 3–4 out of 5/6): The criterion is adequately addressed, though moderate weaknesses are observed.

Very good (score 7–8 out of 10, 6–7 out of 8, or 4–5 out of 5/6): The criterion is well addressed, with only minor shortcomings.

Excellent (score 9–10 out of 10, 8 out of 8, or 5–6 out of 5/6): The criterion is fully addressed, demonstrating outstanding quality with no or only negligible weaknesses.

Threshold per criterion: 3 to 6 points. Overall minimum score: 26 points (out of 42). Maximum total score: 42 points. Proposals failing to reach the threshold in any criterion or the overall minimum score will not be considered for funding.
description:
The Venture Incubation Programme (VIP) serves as an instrument to strengthening incubation capacity in Europe to support early-stage GenAI ventures as well as to:

  1. Accelerate the commercialisation of LLM technologies, providing mentoring, access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources, data infrastructures, and regulatory guidance.
  2. Promote responsible AI innovation, aligned with the AI Act, Data Act, GDPR, and the EU’s Digital Decade Targets.
  3. Foster cross-border collaboration, knowledge sharing, and participation of underrepresented regions and groups in the European AI ecosystem.


Through this call, LLM-BRIDGE seeks to identify and support one high-quality, EU-based incubator capable of supporting startups in the transforming of early-stage GenAI ideas into viable, scalable, and ethically compliant ventures that may be eligible to apply for the future Long Jump and European Grand Challenges. Participating in the VIP provides an opportunity for a leading incubator to position itself at the forefront of Europe’s generative AI revolution. This collaboration offers strategic, reputational, and operational advantages, aligning the incubator with a pan-European initiative that seeks to redefine the future of AI-driven innovation and technological leadership. 

The VIP programme will select one incubator to run a 12-week VIP cohort across Europe, which will:

  1. Deliver structured training and mentoring to 30 startups.
  2. Provide and facilitate access to technical expertise and AI infrastructures.
  3. Monitor and report progress using standardised KPIs defined in the Annex I. 
  4. Contribute to the overall impact of LLM-BRIDGE and the European GenAI innovation ecosystem.

The selected incubator will gain direct access to a carefully selected pipeline of high-potential GenAI startups from across Europe, allowing it to deepen its expertise in nurturing deep-tech ventures with the potential to drive the next wave of generative AI solutions. Such engagement not only enhances the incubators reputation as a leading enabler of cutting-edge innovation but also strengthens its market position within the highly competitive AI ecosystem.

results.summary: EFCSN Permanent Call for Protection Grants
results.content: EFCSN Permanent Call for Protection Grants

beneficiaryAdministration:
Fact-checkers are frequently the targets of attacks and harassment as they speak truth to power. The fact-checking community has been repeatedly harassed: individual fact-checkers and organisations have faced threats, vandalised offices, SLAPPs, and coordinated online hate campaigns designed to censor or cancel their work.

In response, the consortium comprised of the European Fact-Checking Standards Network (EFCSN), together with its members Faktograf, Pagella Politica, Fact Review, FactCheck Cyprus, and Greece Fact Check, has initiated a protection scheme with the support of the European Union.

The primary aim of this scheme is to provide direct, rapid support to fact-checkers in need (e.g. due to online harassment campaigns, hacking attempts, vandalisation of office spaces, threats of physical violence, physical attacks, threats of imprisonment or lawsuits, SLAPPs). Those facing harassment or requiring assistance for their psychological, physical, online or legal safety may submit requests for support under this call. All submissions will be handled with the utmost security and processed as quickly as possible to provide aid to those affected.

Support and Eligible Activities

Fact-checking organisations can request support for the following:

  1. Psychological Support: counselling, burnout prevention, and specialised training. Please note that costs for general staff wellbeing not linked to a specific incident or harassment situation are not eligible.
  2. Legal Aid: defence against defamation, harassment, cyber and physical violence, SLAPP suits, copyright disputes, etc. Please note that legal costs related to commercial disputes, employment matters, or issues unrelated to fact-checking activities are not eligible.
  3. Safe Workspace: this may include installation of security systems, purchase or rental of security equipment, rental of a secure workspace, or costs to enable staff to work remotely during a period of risk. For fact-checkers, the workspace is understood as the reporting assignment itself and the physical space immediately surrounding it.
  4. Emergency Relocation: transport, temporary housing, crisis coordination for teams in danger, etc.
  5. Cybersecurity: upgrades for encryption, security tools, and risk assessments, etc. Please note that general IT infrastructure upgrades not linked to a specific security threat or incident are not eligible.

Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible for funding, applicants must meet the following requirements:

  1. Legal entity: applicants must be a legal entity, whether for-profit or non-profit.
  2. Certification: applicants must be EFCSN certified fact-checking organisations or fact-checking organisations that can demonstrate they respect in practice the European Code of Standards for Independent Fact-Checking Organisations.
  3. Location: organisations must be based in the European Union or DEP-associated countries (see this document for the most up-to-date list).
  4. Single applicants: this call is intended for single applicants, i.e. consortia of organisations cannot apply for this call.

Budget, Funding, Payment Terms, Grant Duration

  1. Total Call Budget: €340,169
  2. Maximum Grant Amount: €20,000 per support request; in exceptional cases (e.g. relocation of a large team), grants can be up to €40,000. Such requests must be reasoned in detail and must be approved by the EFCSN Governance Body in addition to the standard selection procedure outlined below.
  3. Funding Rate: 50%
  4. Form of Grant: lump sums
  5. Number of Grants: ~17
  6. Payment Structure: 75% upon approval of request, 25% following the approval of the final report.
  7. Exact amount must be calculated using this template table.
  8. List of eligible costs:
  9. Direct costs must be directly related to the implementation of the requested support and fall under one of the following categories (although the examples below are not exhaustive):
  10. A. Psychological Support: costs related to mental health, wellbeing support, physical checkups related to long-lasting stress, including counselling sessions, burnout prevention activities, and specialised trauma training provided by qualified professionals.
  11. B. Legal Aid: costs related to legal support services, including legal counsel or lawyer fees, court or filing fees, legal document translation, notary services, and other directly related legal expenses.
  12. C. Physical Safety: costs related to ensuring the physical safety of staff or premises, including security system installation, security equipment purchase or rental, secure workspace rental, remote work setup costs, and related services.
  13. D. Emergency Relocation: costs related to urgent relocation and crisis response, including transport, temporary accommodation, crisis coordination services, subsistence costs during relocation, and related support.
  14. E. Cybersecurity: costs related to digital security and protection, including security software or tool licences, cybersecurity audits or risk assessments, secure hardware (e.g. encrypted devices), implementation and setup costs, and related services.
  15. Retroactive costs: if a grant is approved, costs are eligible from the time of application submission.
  16. Indirect / Administrative costs: these are capped at 10% of total direct costs.
  17. Max. Grant Duration: 12 months
  18. Rolling basis: this call is open on a rolling basis from 2 September 2026 until 31 May 2028 (or until funds are depleted).

Selection Procedure

The evaluation will be conducted in two steps:

Phase 1: AI Processing. The application platform will automatically review submitted applications to ensure that all required information has been provided and that applicants meet the basic eligibility criteria.

Phase 2: Expert Evaluation. Requests will be evaluated by the consortium experts based on need, urgency, regional vulnerability, and the applicant’s capacity to absorb the support. Consortium experts may request additional advice from a multidisciplinary group of experts, comprising the Protection Scheme Advisory Board, and escalate particularly delicate decisions to the EFCSN Governance Body. EFCSN will oversee the process, ensuring transparency, financial safeguards, and equitable distribution. Applications will be assessed against the award criteria outlined below.

The evaluation is conducted in several steps, depending on the amount and urgency of the request, as shown in the image linked here.

The main criteria for evaluating the requests are:

Category

Description

Max. points

Need

Clear evidence of an acute operational or financial gap directly tied to the emergency situation. Financial statements and other documents may be requested as evidence.

10

Urgency

Time-sensitive circumstances where delayed support would meaningfully worsen the outcome.

10

Regional Vulnerability

Context of operating environment: political, economic, or press freedom constraints that amplify risk.

10

Absorptive Capacity

Organisational ability to receive, manage, and account for the funds in a timely manner.

10

How to Apply and Timeline

To apply, please submit your request through the application platform. Requests for urgent support will be processed within 48 hours; other requests will be processed within 5 working days.

Reporting

An outcome report (financial and narrative) is expected from all grant recipients.

Transparency Notice

This call has also been published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal. Funding granted through this call will be disclosed on efcsn.com/funding-opportunities. Disclosure will cover the name of the receiving organisation, amount, and grant duration.

NB! If a grant recipient operates in a high-risk environment or handles sensitive data, they may request that their identity remains confidential during the implementation phase and be disclosed after the end of the funding cycle.

Questions?

Please send questions about this call to grants@efcsn.com.

beneficiaryAdministration:
The European Fact-Checking Standards Network (EFCSN) is pleased to announce a call for Database Grants to support the European fact-checking community in its mission to provide the public with access to trustworthy, fact-checked data.

To that end, the EFCSN, together with its partner organisations Newtral, Science Feedback and Fact Review, is currently building a comprehensive fact-check database: a centralised database of fact-check articles, fact-check data, verified disinformation appearances, and associated metadata. The database will serve various stakeholders as a vital resource going forward and will provide the fact-checking community necessary infrastructure for information exchange, collaboration, and collective licensing.

Successful applicants will be required to set up the necessary workflows and technical infrastructure to contribute to the database. In addition to the grant agreement, they will also be asked to sign a data licensing agreement, enabling the EFCSN to make the data accessible to third parties. In addition to the grant amount, successful applicants will also gain access to the database's backoffice, enabling them to collaborate with other fact-checkers via the platform.

This call is part of the project “Fact-Checkers for European Resilience Against Disinformation (FACTEUR)”, implemented by The European Fact-Checking Standards Network (EFCSN) with seven partner organisations – Pagella Politica/ Facta, Faktograf, Newtral, Fact Review, Greece Fact Check, Fact Check Cyprus and Science Feedback.

Objectives

These grants are designed to support European fact-checking organisations to:

  1. Contribute full text fact-checks from September 21, 2026, onwards until the end of project to a European fact-check database operated by the EFCSN and its partners; successful applicants are encouraged to continue ingesting data after the end of the project; continued data ingestion will be governed by the aforementioned data licensing agreement;
  2. Set up technical infrastructures that may be necessary for contributing to the fact-check database; the Consortium will provide specific options and support for this;
  3. Review AI-generated metadata associated with ingested fact-checks and if necessary correct or annotate data manually;
  4. Grant licensing rights for the data to the EFCSN on the grounds of fair and reasonable conditions;
  5. Promote the database.

Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible for funding, applicants must meet the following requirements:

  1. Legal entity: Applicants must be a legal entity, whether for-profit or non-profit.
  2. Fact-checking: Applicants must be fact-checking organisations or fact-checking teams or units within larger organisations. Fact-checking is defined as the use of an evidence-based method to verify the accuracy of claims made in the public sphere. Applicants must publish at least four human-authored fact-checking articles a month on average. In their editorial work, applicants must have a substantial and demonstrable focus on a country that is a member of the Council of Europe, Kosovo, Belarus or Russia, to apply.
  3. Certification: Applicants must be EFCSN certified fact-checking organisations in order to ensure the highest data quality of the database.
  4. Location: Organisations must be based in the European Union or DEP-associated countries (please consult this document for the most updated version).
  5. Single applicants: This call is intended for single applicants, i.e. consortia of organisations cannot apply for this call.

Budget, Funding, Payment Terms, Grant Duration

  1. Total Call Budget: €860,000.
  2. Maximum Grant Amount: €70,000 per project.
  3. Funding Rate: 50%
  4. Form of Grant: lump sums
  5. Number of Grants: 40-60 grants will be awarded. Exact amount must be calculated using this template table. Grant amounts are calculated based on size of applicant’s organisation and projected number of fact-checks ingested into the database in relation to the total of the entire grantee cohort. At the final reporting stage the actual number of ingested fact-checks will be used to calculate the final payment.
  6. Payment Structure: 40% of the call budget upon grant signatures, 30% following the approval of the interim project reports, 30% following the approval of the final project reports.
  7. List of eligible costs:
  8. direct personnel costs – employees or equivalent: editorial personnel, research personnel, technical personnel, administrative personnel, others; natural persons under direct contract; seconded persons; SME owners and natural person beneficiaries; volunteer costs
  9. subcontracting costs – subcontracting may cover only a limited part of the action (max. 15%).
  10. direct purchase costs – travel and subsistence: accommodation, travels, subsistence; other goods, works and services: consumables, services for meetings and seminars, services for dissemination activities including website, publication fees, other (shipment, insurance, translation, etc.)
  11. Indirect costs – 10%
  12. Grant Duration: 24 months

Selection Procedure

The selection of applications to be funded will be conducted in three distinct phases:

Phase 1: Eligibility & Compliance: The EFCSN team will perform an initial check to ensure all applications are complete, meet the basic requirements and applicants are eligible.

Phase 2: Review: The EFCSN team will review and rate applications based on the following award criteria which will result in a ranking of the applications. All applications that can be covered by the budget can be funded, provided the ranking is approved in Phase 3.

Category

Description

Max Points

Readiness

To what extent the applicant demonstrates a clear commitment to connect their existing editorial systems with the database infrastructure.

10

Capacity

To what extent the applicant demonstrates a proven track record of database work in information integrity and a substantial track record of publishing fact-checks.

10


Phase 3: Final evaluation: The consortium of the FACTEUR project will review the resulting ranking and if appropriate approve it.

How to apply and timeline

To apply, please fill out this application form on the EFCSN Grants Platform. Note that you will need to register an account if you have not already.

The call opens on 29 July 2026 and closes on 20 September 2026 at 23:59. Evaluations will take place at the end of September 2026, results will be communicated shortly afterwards.

Transparency notice

This call has also been published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.

Funding granted through this call will be disclosed on: https://efcsn.com/funding-opportunities/. Disclosure will cover the name of the receiving organisation, amount, and grant duration.

Questions?

Please send questions about this call to grants@efcsn.com.

description:
Basic information

AENAON implements two competitive Open Call rounds through its Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) scheme. The Open Calls aim to maximise the uptake, integration, testing and validation of AENAON technologies and services, including the Federated Digital Twin-based Cyber Range Platform, cybersecurity training capabilities and cybersecurity preparedness services, in realistic offshore wind and related critical-infrastructure environments.

The Open Calls are designed to engage SMEs and start-ups, large enterprises and technology providers, research organisations and universities, cybersecurity service and technology providers, offshore wind operators, manufacturers and supply-chain actors, energy and critical-infrastructure stakeholders, and other relevant innovation actors. Supported third-party projects are expected to contribute practical use cases, validation evidence, technical feedback and sector-relevant results that strengthen the cybersecurity and resilience of the offshore wind ecosystem.

Open Call 1 focuses on the initial validation, integration and testing of AENAON technologies and services in realistic environments. Activities may include the development and validation of sector-specific cybersecurity scenarios, identification and assessment of offshore-wind-relevant vulnerabilities, integration with simulation and cyber range environments, cybersecurity testing and training activities, and validation of cybersecurity tools, services and preparedness capabilities.

Open Call 1 sub-projects are expected to have an implementation period of 8 months, with clearly defined tasks, milestones, deliverables, KPIs and acceptance evidence.

Applicants may propose activities related to cybersecurity testing and validation, cyber range training and scenario-based exercises, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, threat and risk assessment, risk monitoring, cyberattack management, digital twin-based validation and integration, or other cybersecurity resilience use cases that are demonstrably aligned with the objectives and technical capabilities of AENAON.

Budget

The total AENAON FSTP budget is €4,100,000.

The indicative allocation is:

  1. €2,100,000 for Open Call 1
  2. €2,000,000 for Open Call 2

Any amount not committed under Open Call 1 may be reallocated to Open Call 2, subject to budget availability, the applicable Open Call rules and the principles of transparency, equal treatment and sound financial management.

Funding Constraints

AENAON will provide sub-grants under two Open Calls (Open Call 1 and 2), with a total FSTP allocation of €4,100,000. In line with the call topic, the scheme derogates from the €60k ceiling, allowing up to €100,000 per individual third party (only in the case of offshore wind farm operators and manufacturers, which are considered large critical infrastructures/ operators of essential services) and up to €150,000 per action (in case of small consortia).

Example 1 — SME A, Open Call 1

  1. Entity A is a generic SME, applicable ceiling: €60,000
  2. Funding requested/awarded in Open Call 1: €55,000
  3. Result: Eligible (Remaining funding capacity for Open Call 2 under AENAON: €5,000, if applicable)

Example 2 — Offshore wind-farm operator B, Open Call 1

  1. Entity B is an offshore wind-farm operator and therefore benefits from the derogated ceiling; applicable ceiling: €100,000
  2. Funding awarded in Open Call 1: €87,000
  3. Result: Eligible (Remaining funding capacity for Open Call 2: €13,000, if applicable)

Example 3 — Small consortium B + C, Open Call 2

  1. In Open Call 2, B and C form a small consortium. B = offshore wind-farm operator/manufacturer, and C = SME, thus, maximum funding per consortium action: €150,000.
  2. However, the individual ceilings must also be respected. Since B already received €87,000 in Open Call 1, B can receive only €100,000 − €87,000 = €13,000
  3. C has received no previous AENAON funding. Therefore, C can receive up to €60,000
  4. The total maximum eligible AENAON funding for the consortium (B+C) in Open Call 2 is therefore €73,000 (B up to €13,000, C up to €60,000)
  5. Consortium action (budget requested): €73k < €150k maximum per action

The final lump-sum amount awarded to each selected third-party beneficiary will be fixed at the contracting stage through a needs-based, auditable right-sizing process, taking into account the proposed activities, technical complexity, budget needs, expected contribution to AENAON objectives, evaluation outcome, milestones, deliverables, and acceptance criteria.

Payment Schedule

AENAON applies a staged payment model of 30% – 40% – 30%:

  1. 30% initial payment upon signature of the Sub-Grant Agreement and completion of onboarding requirements
  2. 40% interim payment following successful completion of the mid-term review and acceptance of required interim reports, deliverables and supporting evidence
  3. 30% final payment following completion of the action and acceptance of the final report, final deliverables, performance evidence and required outputs

Payments are conditional upon the satisfactory achievement of agreed milestones, deliverables and acceptance criteria. Payments may be suspended, reduced or recovered in cases of non-performance, breach of contractual obligations, false declarations, conflict of interest, ineligible activities or serious non-compliance with reporting, ethics, GDPR, visibility or audit requirements.

callTitle: Financial support for Finnish micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises to promote the commercialisation of innovative cybersecurity solutions
furtherInformation:
The call is open to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises registered in Finland.

Financial support may be provided for projects that aim to promote market readiness and commercialisation of innovative cybersecurity solutions. Financial support may be granted for example piloting, optimizing and other development measures supporting market readiness of the solution, as well as for other measures promoting the commercialization, market entry, uptake and determining the preconditions for internationalisation of a product or service.

Only innovative cybersecurity solutions with a high technological readiness level (TRL) shall be financed. Marketing actions, other sales promotion actions or export aid or aid contingent upon the use of domestic goods or services over imported one shall not be financed.

Financial support of a minimum of EUR 10,000 and a maximum of EUR 100,000 may be granted per project. There is a 30 % self-financing (co-funding) requirement per project. 70 % of the financial support is paid after the administrative funding decision and 30 % after the project report and actually incurred costs have been approved by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom. 

You can find more information about the terms and conditions on the NCC-FI website: https://www.kyberturvallisuuskeskus.fi/en/our-activities/national-coordination-centre-cyber-security-research-development-and-innovation

The proposal will include the mandatory annexes and any other annexes that the applicants decide to attach in order to demonstrate the eligibility, quality and applicability of the results, the suitability of the proposed mechanism for their application in the context of sustainability, or other parameters of the project.

For each project, a member of the NCC-CZ Council will be appointed by the NCC-CZ Council to manage the evaluation process, based on the submission and the sectoral focus of the project. As part of the evaluation, the NCC-CZ administrators will assess the formal compliance of the submitted project proposal with the requirements of the call and will carry out an assessment of the acceptability of the project in terms of the substantive requirements for projects. description:
The aim of the call is to support the creation, development and practical validation of scalable solutions that address the documented needs of the Czech cybersecurity ecosystem. Supported projects must combine design or development, at least one pilot deployment or practical validation, evaluation of results and preparation for further use. The call is focused on three thematic areas:

The call is focused on three main thematic pillars:

• Scalable solutions for the resilience of small and medium-sized enterprises: new or significantly expanded services and tools to protect small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), self-assessment, prioritisation of measures and sector- specific implementation packages.

• Implementation tools and services for compliance readiness, management and risk management: practical solutions for NIS2, CRA, DORA, supply chain security, cybersecurity management, record-keeping, reporting, secure development, SBOM and vulnerability management.

• Services and technical solutions for incident preparedness, response and recovery: standardised services, sector-specific scenarios, exercise packages and tools for recovery testing, record-keeping, escalation and reporting.

Support will be given primarily to projects that aim to deliver solutions with a measurable impact on a wider target group. Analyses alone, general training or documentation without implementation and validation activities are not a priority. Implementation by individual organisations is eligible primarily as a means of piloting the transferability and wider applicability of the results.

furtherInformation:
In accordance with the programme’s terms and conditions, the maximum amount of financial support is €100,000 and the minimum amount is €60,000 (in the form of a grant),depending on the current exchange rate of the Czech koruna. Projects will be funded at a rate of 50% of eligible costs, which means that the beneficiary will receive funding amounting to one half of the eligible costs incurred during the implementation of the project and substantiated in accordance with the established rules. The funding awarded to a project may be lower than the amount that was requested in the application. The decision on the final amount of support granted will depend on the quality of the project application, the consistency of the expected results with the proposed budget, and the structure of the individual planned costs.

Beneficiaries will be required to regularly provide evidence of actual expenditure incurred in connection with the implementation of the project. Details regarding the frequency and format of reporting will be specified in the grant agreement. Applicants must ensure that the project proposal meets the conditions designed to prevent the project funding from resulting in unauthorised indirect state aid within the meaning of relevant European legislation, or from leading to double funding.

The following types of organisations are eligible to participate in this call and meet the criteria set out in the EU Digital Europe programme:

• Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

• Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) that demonstrate professional competence and the ability to produce and practically validate an output in line with the objectives of the call.

• Academic and research institutions are eligible only as members of a consortium that includes at least one small or medium-sized enterprise. They may not submit an application on their own.

Consortia may combine the above-mentioned entities. The application must specify the actual roles, responsibilities and budgets of the members; a formal partnership without evidence of added value is not sufficient.

callTitle: Strengthening European Cybersecurity Technologies, Capacities and Preparedness
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

  • Support the adoption of market-ready innovative AI-powered cybersecurity solutions, including solutions developed in the framework of EU-supported research and innovation projects.
  • Provide and deploy up to date AI-powered tools and services to organisations (in particular SMEs) to prepare, protect and respond to cybersecurity threats.
  • Integrate AI technologies into cybersecurity processes to improve the security of ICT solutions, including providing innovative approaches to training employees to use AI solutions for cybersecurity.
  • Deployment of cybersecure tools and technologies relying on trustworthy AI; AI driven cybersecurity tools; Integration of tools to protect and secure AI solutions.

Objective:

To support the market uptake and dissemination of innovative AI-powered cybersecurity solutions (notably in SMEs, possibly using results stemming from Horizon Europe projects or similar) and improve knowledge and auditing of cybersecurity preparedness.

SMEs often lack the resources to assess cyber risks, develop cybersecurity strategies and implement solutions, leaving them vulnerable to cyberattacks. The resilience of organisations that fall into this category is key to the prosperity of the EU single market.

Cyber risk assessment and management can be significantly enhanced and simplified with the application of AI-based tools and solutions. However, this requires an understanding of the evolving technology landscape, of the benefits of technology integration and of deployment prioritisation. Faced with organisational and financial constraints, the SMEs may be missing the opportunity to fully harness AI-powered solutions to advance their cybersecurity and resilience.

Cybersecurity is the precondition for reliable, secure and resilient AI models and algorithms. Cybersecurity of AI is not just about protecting AI systems against threats such as poisoning and evasion attacks, as it also involves ensuring they have trustworthiness features such as human oversight and robustness – the ability to resist cyberattacks, as required by the EU’s AI Act for high-risk AI systems. The need for human oversight of AI has also been emphasised by experts. Also, the use of AI at the SME level supporting the integration of predictive algorithms can greatly support to a bottom-up approach when dealing with vulnerability detections, threat mitigation and more efficient coordinated incident response.

Scope:

This action aims to increase the maturity of cyber risk management and improve the cyber resilience and ultimately foster a technologically advanced culture of cybersecurity for SMEs in the EU. Actions in this topic should develop and deploy AI-powered products, tools and services for European SMEs, also enabling the detection/discovery of attack patterns.

Proposals should cover the development or adaptation of the software/hardware and the validation of the solutions.

It foresees the automation of fundamental cybersecurity processes, in particular in small market organisations, through a SaaS toolkit tailored to the needs of SMEs. This toolkit should allow SMEs to improve the key aspects of their cybersecurity by providing user-friendly tools for risk management [1], threat detection, incident response and notification, to improve their cyber hygiene and mitigate potential threats while protecting personal data. The cyber toolkit should also provide cyber-incident prediction and response functions to improve SMEs’ resilience.

Activities should include at least one of the following:

  • Uptake/adoption of AI-powered cybersecurity tools in organisations where this has not yet taken place.
  • Development of user-friendly sets of tools (e.g. toolkit) based on AI to automate main cybersecurity processes in SMEs. Such a toolkit could provide automated functions such as:
    • A function that supports the assessment and management of an SME’s cybersecurity risks. This function should perform a risk assessment, provide recommendations for risk mitigation, and identify options.
    • An interface to existing tools that support the analysis and assessment of the extent of an SME’s cyber risk based on information gathered from digital infrastructure scanning and data provided by authorised users.
    • A function that issues alerts on relevant vulnerabilities and threats based on the information collected by the risk management function.
    • A function that connects SMEs to a Cyber Hub to report an incident and assist with recovery if possible.
  • SME user interface for incident reporting associated with the cyber toolkit. Users can report an incident, get instructions on how to react and obtain information on how to obtain support for the response, with the use of AI assistants.

[1] Interoperable EU Risk Management Framework, ENISA, 2023, available at: https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/interoperable-eu-risk-management-framework

title: Coordinated preparedness testing and other preparedness actions
callTitle: Strengthening European Cybersecurity Technologies, Capacities and Preparedness
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

The types of deliverables are presented in two parts.

The first part covers:

  • Enhanced cooperation, preparedness and cybersecurity resilience in the EU; preparedness support services.
  • Threat assessment and risk assessment services.

The second part covers:

  • Risk monitoring services
  • Better compliance, coordinated vulnerability disclosure and monitoring
  • Improved skills, via exercises and training courses, organisation of events, workshops. Stakeholder consultations and white papers.

Objective:

This action covers two actions from the Cyber Solidarity Act, dedicated to the Cybersecurity Emergency Mechanism, namely (1) coordinated preparedness testing of entities operating in sectors of high criticality across the Union and (2) other preparedness actions for entities operating in sectors of high criticality and other critical sectors.

Objectives

These actions aim to complement and not duplicate efforts by Member States and those at Union level to increase the level of protection and resilience to cyber threats, in particular for critical industrial installations and infrastructures, by assisting Member States in their efforts to improve their preparedness for cyber threats and incidents by providing them with knowledge and expertise.

Proposals should contribute to achieving at least one of the following objectives:

  • (part 1) Coordinated preparedness testing of entities operating in sectors of high criticality across the Union (including penetration testing and threat assessment) considering ICT as well as Operational Technology/Industrial Control Systems.
  • (part 2) Other preparedness actions for entities operating in sectors of high criticality and other critical sectors (i.e. vulnerability monitoring, exercises and training courses).

For details on the actions related to (part 1) and (part 2) covered under the current call for proposals, please consult the Call document accordingly.

Scope:

[Part 1 Coordinated preparedness testing]

The provision of preparedness support services shall include the activities listed below, for entities in the sector or sub-sector as identified by the Commission in accordance with the Cyber Solidarity Act, from the Sectors of High Criticality listed in Annex I to Directive (EU) 2022/2555 and specified in the call for proposal document for each of the calls under this topic:

Support for testing for potential vulnerabilities:

  • Development of penetration testing scenarios. The proposed scenarios may cover Networks, Applications, Virtualisation solutions, Cloud solutions, Industrial Control systems, and IoT.
  • Support for conducting testing of essential entities operating critical infrastructure for potential vulnerabilities.
  • Support for the deployment of digital tools and infrastructures supporting the execution of testing scenarios and for conducting exercises such as the development of standardised cyber-ranges or other testing facilities, able to mimic features of critical sectors (e.g. energy sector, transport sector, etc.) or others affected by NIS 2 to facilitate the execution of cyber-exercises, in particular within cross-border scenarios where relevant.
  • Evaluation and/or testing of cybersecurity capabilities of MS entities and MS sectors (including capabilities to prevent, detect and respond to incidents and stress test of the entire sectors), evaluation and compliance activities aimed at increasing maturity, e.g. on the basis of established maturity models and/or relevant evaluation and compliance schemes.
  • Evaluation and/or testing of cybersecurity capabilities of entities in scope (including for the evaluation and management of risks concerning the supply chain).
  • Consulting services, providing recommendations on how to improve infrastructure security and capabilities.

Support for threat assessment and risk assessment, such as:

  • Threat Assessment process implementation and life cycle
  • Customised risk scenarios analysis.

The support will target the competent authorities in the Member States, which play a central role in the implementation of the NIS2 Directive, such as Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) and National Cybersecurity Authorities.

[Part 2 other preparedness actions]

For the second part, in addition to the services already listed for Part 1 (support for testing for potential vulnerabilities and support for threat assessment and risk management), the provision of preparedness support services included below addresses entities operating in highly critical and other critical sectors as referred to in Annex I and II of the NIS 2 Directive.

Support for threat assessment and risk assessment:

  • Supply chain risk management within the risk assessment services.

Risk monitoring service:

  • Specific continuous risk monitoring such as attack surface monitoring, risk monitoring of assets and vulnerabilities.

Support coordinated vulnerability disclosure and management:

  • Promote the adoption of national CVD Policies [1] and the EU Vulnerability Database.
  • Coordinate the disclosure of vulnerabilities and timely dissemination of security patches. Standardisation of the way information is shared between different stakeholders in the vulnerability handling process.
  • CVD applications that manage multiple sources of vulnerability information using open standards or technologies. (e.g. researchers, vendors, CSIRTs).
  • Raise awareness on the adoption of vulnerability management best practices.

Dedicated exercises and training courses:

  • Develop [2] comprehensive training programmes and workshops, including international ones, for cybersecurity professionals that will cover the latest trends in cyber threats, attack methodologies, and best practices for pre-threat management and prevention. Maturity checks, evaluation of cybersecurity capabilities.
  • Encourage the development of cybersecurity continuous learning activities [3] to keep up with all cybersecurity requirements driven by EU cybersecurity-related regulations and directives, including the NIS 2 Directive, CSA, CSoA, DORA, EECC, GDPR, CRA.

The support will target the competent authorities in the Member States, which play a central role in the implementation of the NIS2 Directive, Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) including sectorial CSIRTs, Security Operation Centres (SOC)/Cyber Hubs, highly critical and other critical sectors, industry stakeholders (including Information Sharing and Analysis Centres- ISACs) and any other actors within the scope of the NIS 2 Directive, DORA, CSA, etc.

Support may be provided, among others, for the on boarding to the CEF Cybersecurity Core Service Platforms of public and private organisations which are working on the implementation of the NIS 2 Directive and are potential users of the CEF Cybersecurity Core Service Platforms.

The action may also support industry, with a particular focus on start-ups and SMEs, to seize the industrial and market uptake opportunities created by the Cyber Resilience Act and may support the implementation of the NIS 2 Directive.

[1] Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Policies in the EU, ENISA, 2022, available at: https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure-policies-in-the-eu

[2] Based on the European Cybersecurity Skills Framework (ECSF)

[3] Based on ECSF: https://www.enisa.europa.eu/topics/education/european-cybersecurity-skills-framework

title: Cybersecure tools, technologies and services relying on AI
callTitle: Strengthening European Cybersecurity Technologies, Capacities and Preparedness
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

  • Deployment of Artificial Intelligence and various AI-powered technologies as enablers for Cyber Hubs, CSIRTs, NCSCs, NIS SPOCs and others.
  • Novel cybersecurity tools based on AI that have been developed, tested and validated in relevant conditions and made available to Cyber Hubs, CSIRTs, NCSCs, NIS SPOCs and others.
  • Enhanced information sharing and collaboration amongst National and Cross-Border Cyber Hubs, CSIRTs, NCSCs, NIS SPOCs and others relevant stakeholders, supported by CTI produced by AI-powered tools.
  • Tools for automation of cybersecurity processes such as the creation, analysis and processing of CTI, to enhance operations of the Cyber Hubs.
  • Original European CTI feeds or services.
  • Ensure that the most advanced and innovative secure AI solutions are developed and implemented for NIS sectors.
  • Secure AI solutions and tools, complying with EU legislation. Promote the mitigation of risks associated with the misuse of AI by malicious actors, with a focus on AI ethics and secure deployment.
  • Contribution to the standardisation and certification of cybersecure, trustworthy AI technologies.

Objective:

This topic addresses AI-based technologies (including GenAI) for national authorities and competent authorities, including National and Cross-Border Cyber Hubs, CSIRTs, public bodies and private entities from the NIS 2 directive, NCCs [1], etc. They play a key role in providing central operational capacity to European cybersecurity ecosystems. They may also provide primary input data for AI/ML-based cybersecurity tools and solutions, which can strengthen such authorities’ capacity to analyse, detect and prevent cyber threats and incidents, and to support the production of high-quality intelligence on cyber threats. In particular, the adoption of generative AI [2] could be a challenge and an opportunity for cybersecurity [3] processes and applications.

These enabling technologies should allow for more effective creation and analysis of Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI), automation of large-scale processes, as well as faster and scalable processing of CTI and identification of patterns that allow for rapid detection and decision making.

The security of AI itself, especially for the systems in the learning phase, also needs to be addressed, including the misuse of AI by malicious actors. This includes carrying out risk assessments and mitigation of cybersecurity risks inherent to AI technologies, implementing supply chain security, etc., and complying with the AI Act, intellectual property legislation and the GDPR.

In addition to being secure, the AI technologies being developed should perform well, and be robust and trustworthy. In particular, having trustworthy AI solutions will help in the deployment phase, where social acceptance is essential.

[1] If applicable and in line with individual national strategies.

[2] Cybersecurity in the age of generative AI, September 2023, available at: https://www.mckinsey.com/featured insights/themes/cybersecurity-in-the-age-of-generative-ai.

[3] The Need For AI-Powered Cybersecurity to Tackle AI-Driven Cyberattacks, April 2024, available at: https://www.isaca.org/resources/news-and-trends/isaca-now-blog/2024/the-need-for-ai-powered cybersecurity-to-tackle-ai-driven-cyberattacks.

Scope:

Actions in this topic should develop and deploy systems and tools for cybersecurity[1], based on AI technologies[2], addressing aspects such as threat detection, vulnerability detection, threat mitigation, incident recovery through self-healing, data analysis and data sharing. These activities must also comply with intellectual property rights (IPR) and the GDPR, depending on the type of information handled. The AI solutions proposed should also be cybersecure.

Activities should include at least one of the following:

  • Continuous detection of patterns and identification of anomalies that can potentially indicate emerging threats, recognising new attack vectors and enabling advanced detection in an evolving threat landscape, including in ICT or in Operational Technology infrastructures using open technologies.
  • Creation of CTI based on novel threat detection capabilities
  • Enhancing speed of incident response through real-time monitoring of networks to identify security incidents and generating alerts or triggering automated responses.
  • Mitigating malware threats by analysing code behaviour, network traffic, and file characteristics, reducing the window of opportunity for attackers to exploit malware.
  • Identification of vulnerabilities and support for management considering multiple sources of information.
  • Cybersecure tools and solutions that provide risk-reduction in the crossover between AI, IoT and smart grids or other manufacturing chains.
  • Support for recovery from incidents through self-healing capacities.
  • Reducing the chances of attacks and pre-emptively identifying weaknesses through automated vulnerability scanning and penetration testing.
  • Protecting business sensitive data through the analysis of access patterns and detection of abnormal behaviour.
  • Enabling organisations to leverage and share CTI and other actionable information for analysis and insights without compromising data security and privacy, through anonymisation.
  • Tools and solutions that provide product security or cybersecurity by design/default in line with CRA requirements.
  • Tool and service providers are welcome to apply for this topic, also when in a consortium with Cyber Hubs. Links with stakeholders in the area of High-Performance Computing should be made where appropriate, as well as activities to foster networking with such stakeholders. In well justified cases, access requests to the EuroHPC high performance computing infrastructure could be granted.
  • The systems, tools and services developed under this topic will be made available for licensing to National and/or Cross-Border Cyber Hubs platforms, CSIRTs, competent authorities, and other relevant authorities under favourable market conditions.
  • These actions aim at providing AI-powered cybersecurity capabilities for National and/or Cross-Border Cyber Hubs and for national authorities encompassing Cyber Hubs, CSIRTs, which occupy a central role in ensuring the cybersecurity of national authorities, providers of critical infrastructures and essential services. These entities are tasked with monitoring, understanding and proactively managing cybersecurity threats. In light of their crucial operative role in ensuring cybersecurity in the Union, the nature of the technologies involved as well as the sensitivity of the information handled, Cyber Hubs must be protected against possible dependencies and vulnerabilities in cybersecurity to pre-empt foreign influence and control.
  • Tools to protect and secure AI solutions in line with the EU legislative framework and considering integration of requirements for robustness, performance, trust and balanced AI autonomy.
  • Contribute to the cybersecurity certification of AI-driven cybersecurity solutions and systems. The primary objective of cybersecurity certification for AI systems within the EU is twofold: to mitigate cybersecurity risks inherent in AI technologies and to demonstrate compliance with the EU’s comprehensive legislative framework, including the AI Act. By establishing a standardised, transparent, and rigorous certification process, the EU seeks to foster trust in AI technologies among users, developers, and regulators alike.

[1] Multilayer Framework for Good Cybersecurity Practices for AI, ENISA, June 2023, available at: https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/multilayer-framework-for-good-cybersecurity-practices-for-ai.

[2] Cybersecurity of AI and Standardisation, ENISA, March 2023, available at: https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/cybersecurity-of-ai-and-standardisation.
